Where WebMCP is still an origin trial, the published pages carry the trial token for `rapier.website` alone; a self-hosted copy needs its own origin's token (an `Origin-Trial` response header). Without the permission or the API the door registers nothing and `status().failures` names each tool's refusal; the door's own re-check at execution (connection, admission, the registering document) stands regardless. The tools belong to the document that registered them: the door registers on `document.modelContext`, never on `window`, keeps no catalog outside that document, and retires every registration when the registering context changes. WebMCP's lifecycle events (`toolactivated`, `toolcancel` on `document.modelContext`) name a tool, not an invocation. Rapier binds request receipts and cancellation to its own invocation identities; source acts retain their canonical transaction IDs.

MCP Apps receives worker `_meta.ui.csp` instead, including the configured download domains and resource origin, and asks its host for clipboard-write permission. Its resource carries a sensitive editor key, is private/TTL-zero, and belongs to the Apps host's trust model. The `rapier-html` wrapper inserts carried data into the supplied page; it does not set an HTTP CSP, accept parent origins, fetch a return address, or authorize generic iframe commands.

## 5. What is checked, and what is not

Verification protects the host grant, current document and port, exact source, confirmed saves, retained
picture bytes, stale-work refusal and Undo. The retained `agent-door-admission` and `generic-client-authority`
rows cover those owners and their MessageChannel exchanges. Picture checks preserve bytes, hashes, URL source
and the local preview's network boundary. The helper's retained cells cover transport and form-value custody.

A Node-only run does not execute a built-browser cell. A same-origin iframe does not prove native WebMCP
discovery or cross-origin CSP enforcement, and a build receipt establishes assembly only. Report the actual
rows and host paths exercised. Browser sandbox enforcement, recovery controls and a real host's storage
durability require their own evidence; these contracts do not establish them by assertion.

# https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/blob/main/docs/markdown-standard.md

# Self-contained Markdown

**Open convention · v1**

One UTF-8 `.md` file holds the document and every image: CommonMark with GFM tables, task lists and strikethrough,
plus the conventions below, each an inline HTML element, HTML comment or reference definition. [Will/1](will.md) is
separate. Other syntax: [Markdown profile](markdown-profile.md).

## Measured against the specification

Corpora: the 652 [CommonMark 0.31.2](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/) examples and the 677 examples of the
published [GFM 0.29 specification](https://github.github.com/gfm/) (28 extension examples). Open, save, a middle
edit, Undo and Redo leave all 1,329 sources exactly as they were.

| Measure | CommonMark | GFM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parser output, every Rapier extension on, official HTML normalization | 643 of 652 (98.62%) | 664 of 677 (98.08%) |
| Semantic renderer and styled HTML writer against the unadjusted official meaning | 638 of 652 (97.85%) | 662 of 677 (97.78%) |
| Document meaning kept under the [documented profile](markdown-profile.md) | 652 of 652 | 677 of 677 |

Differences: GFM autolinks and the disallowed-tag filter also apply in core examples; tasks stay interactive; table
alignment is CSS; HTML comments follow CommonMark 0.31.2; opening front matter and the complete-tag rule for raw HTML
differ. Meaning is words, structure, code and language ids, link destinations, image descriptions, checked state and
column alignment, under the document's HTML safety policy. No example is skipped.

## Layout

A layout comment ends a paragraph or heading. A picture with layout is alone in its paragraph. `<payload>` is Base64
image bytes.

```md
## A right-aligned heading <!--md-layout:v1 align=right-->

![Site photograph][photo] <!--md-layout:v1 width=47% wrap=around x=72% y=2.4em-->

Following prose can flow above, beside and below the picture.

[photo]: data:image/jxl;base64,<payload>
```

| Field | Values | On | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `left`, `center`, `right`, `justify` | text, picture | Alignment. `justify`: text only. |
| `width` | `N%`, above 0, at most 100 | picture | Width in the content box. |
| `lines` | Integer, 1 to 12 | paragraph, picture | N lines tall (see "The line"). Not with `width`. |
| `wrap` | `around`, `beside`, `box`, `behind`, `front` | picture | Text follows the silhouette, one side of the rectangle, or the turned rectangle; or the picture is out of flow, under or over the words. |
| `x` | `N%`, 0 to 100 | picture | Horizontal center. Needs `width` or `wrap`. |
| `y` | `Nem`, signed, at least -50 | picture | Top inset in the anchor, in its font size. Needs `wrap`. |
| `rotate` | `Ndeg`, signed, one decimal at most, above -180, at most 180 | picture | Clockwise turn about the center. |
| `opacity` | `N%`, integer, 5 to 100 | picture | Opacity. Bytes never change. |
| `lock` | `on` | picture | Rapier: a tap goes to the words; a hold takes the picture. |
| `first` | `N`, signed, nonzero, six decimals at most, -64 to 64 | paragraph | First-line indent, in `2em` levels of the body type. |
| `indent` | As `first` | text | Block indent from the start edge, in `2em` levels of the body type. |
| `marker` | As `first` | list item's leading paragraph | Marker offset toward the words, in `2em` levels. Moves no words. |
| `hyphens` | `auto` | paragraph | Hyphenation, refined breaks, bounded word spacing. |
| `caps` | `small` | paragraph | Real small capitals on the first line; an initial keeps its capital. |
| `hanging` | `on` | paragraph | Punctuation may hang into the margin. |
| `before` | `Npt`, 0 to 720, two decimals at most | text, picture | Space above, replacing `spacing` (Word Spacing Before). |
| `after` | As `before` | text, picture | Space below (Word Spacing After). Adjacent blocks use the larger of `after` and `before`. |
| `line` | `N`, 0.5 to 4; or `Npt` or `Npt+`, above 0, at most 720; two decimals at most | text | Multiple of the type size, exact height, or minimum height (Word Multiple, Exactly, At least). |

Text is paragraphs and headings. A heading ignores `first`.

**Picture modes.**

1. Normal flow: `width` or `lines`, with `align` or `x`. `x` needs `width`.
2. Wrapped: `wrap=around`, `beside` or `box`, with `width`, `x`, `y`.
3. Out of flow: `wrap=behind` or `front`, with `width`, `x`, `y`. Text lays out as if the picture were absent.

- `align` excludes `wrap` and `x`.
- `rotate` and `opacity` combine with any mode, and never change the flow.
- Normal-flow `x` reserves no space and keeps source order.
- A writer that changes `spacing` for every block removes `before`, `after` and `line` from every marker.

**Rotation.** A raster or a foreign SVG carries `rotate` and keeps its bytes. It reserves its turned bounding box,
`w·|cos|+h·|sin|` by `w·|sin|+h·|cos|`, on the same center. An editable drawing turns its geometry instead.

**Defaults.**

- No `align`: the block's first-strong direction (`dir=auto`). `left` and `right` are physical.
- No `width` or `lines`: intrinsic width, at most `min(1, r, 1.6 / (1 + 1/r))` of the column in the reference
  renderer, for aspect ratio `r`.
- No `x` with `wrap`: the left edge.
- Renderers clamp the displayed rectangle without rewriting source.

**Anchor.** A picture's anchor is the next text block in its container, else the previous one, skipping picture and
empty paragraphs.

- Paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, callouts, definition lists and details anchor. Tables, code, figures,
  mathematics and rules are barriers.
- `y` is from the anchor's content top, clamped to its unwrapped height. Crossing into another block changes the
  anchor and rebases `y`.
- With no anchor, the picture stays in normal flow.

**Wrapping.**

- Text flows above, beside (each free side) and below, in source order.
- The silhouette is image alpha or drawing geometry. A rectangle is a valid fallback; `box` turns with a turned
  drawing.
- Paragraphs and headings flow around the picture. Lists, quotes and details shorten their lines and stay whole.
  Tables, code, rules, figures and mathematics stay whole.
- `behind` paints under the words, undimmed; `front`, over them.

### Attachment and writing

**Grammar.** One line: `<!--md-layout:v1`, `key=value` fields separated by spaces or tabs, optional horizontal
whitespace, `-->`. Tabs and printable ASCII only. Each key once.

- `N` is digits, optionally `.` and digits. No leading zeros except `0`, no `+`, no exponent, no `°`.
- Only signed fields take `-`. Zero is never signed (`-0em`, `-0deg` are invalid).

**Attachment.** A marker is the last meaningful inline token of its paragraph or heading: before closing hashes in
an ATX heading, before the underline in a Setext heading, and likewise in nested paragraphs.

- `marker` needs the list item's first block to be a paragraph.
- Picture fields need a paragraph of one picture, optionally in one link.
- `hyphens`, `caps` and `hanging` never apply in a table cell.
- A standalone comment, and any comment in code, governs nothing.

**Invalid.** An unknown version, key or value, a repeated key, a misplaced marker, or two layout comments in a block:
the marker is inert and kept, and the picture shows inline, upright, at natural size.

**Writing.**

- Lowercase keys, one space apart, in this order:
  `align width lines wrap x y rotate opacity first indent marker lock hyphens caps hanging before after line`.
- No trailing decimal zeros. Omit `y=0em`, `rotate=0deg`, `opacity=100%`, and an empty marker.
- Only an intentional edit changes source.

**In tables.** A measured paragraph a GFM cell cannot hold is HTML: `text-indent` and `margin-inline-start` in points;
a list's `li` carries the marker offset, its leading paragraph subtracts it, and a nested list cancels it. The native
writer also reads `em` relative to the body type.

### Conformance rungs

**Rung 0: any CommonMark reader.** Comments are hidden; pictures show inline, upright and solid.

**Rung 1: position and size in CSS.** `align`, `first`, `indent`, `marker`, `width`, `x`, `opacity`, `lines` (see
"The line"; an initial letter uses `initial-letter`), and `hyphens`, `caps`, `hanging` through the reference
stylesheet's selectors. `rotate` without `wrap` stays upright.

**Rung 2: placement in CSS.**

| `wrap` | CSS |
| --- | --- |
| `around` | `float: left` when `x` is absent or below 50%, else `right`; `shape-outside: url(<the picture>)`; `shape-image-threshold` near 10%. |
| `beside`, `box` | The same float, no `shape-outside`. |
| `behind`, `front` | Positioned by `x`, `y`, `width`; `z-index` below or above the text. |

A turned picture uses a CSS `transform` and supplies its turned shape: `shape-outside: polygon(...)` from the turned
box's corners, or for `box` and `beside` a float of that size. Rung 2 has no words on both sides or inside a picture.

**Rung 3: Rapier's planner,** in `rapier-markdown-kit` ([standard-adoption](standard-adoption.md), "The drop-in
module"): both-sides and interior wrapping, the reference scale, deterministic for the same measured input. Below rung
3, exact line breaks are recommended, not required.

#### Rich wrapping reference engine

The planner uses one [Pretext snapshot](https://github.com/chenglou/pretext/tree/0d102a5cd933611e86a7e60bda7b4baa5995c6b0),
Pretext 1.0.0 plus main through pull request #525, with Canvas measurement.

- Admitted: Chrome and Chromium. Native wrapping: Firefox, WebKit, Chrome on iOS, unsupported shaping or settings,
  complex objects, authored `br`, preserved whitespace, balanced headings, authored `text-wrap:pretty`, soft-break
  tokens, fragments and `scripts:false` pages.
- Greedy picture flow. A lone Latin, Greek or Cyrillic word prefix, or a no-break-space group, may move to a wider
  slot on the same row.
- Fragments give `sourceStart` and `sourceEnd`, UTF-16 offsets in the item's original text. Not every segment
  boundary is a break.
- Nothing engine-specific is saved. Offline pages carry the code and its notices.

### The line

`--md-line` is the body's line box. `linestretch` sets it.

`lines=N` sets a picture like `initial-letter`: top at the first line's cap height, foot on the Nth baseline, height
`calc((N - 1) * var(--md-line) + 1cap)`, width by aspect ratio. With `wrap`, `y` insets from the cap height; in
normal flow, the picture's own paragraph sets line and cap.

```md
![W][initial] <!--md-layout:v1 lines=5 wrap=around-->

ith a decorative letter the paragraph opens on five lines, at any text size.
```

- Baseline below the line top: `(line - (ascent + descent)) / 2 + ascent`.
- Export measures the font at the printable width; without it, the cap is 0.7 of the body.
- Resized beside its words, the picture snaps to whole lines; elsewhere it takes `width`.

### Paragraph typography

```md
---
lang: en-AU
---

With a letter capital the paragraph opens on three lines. <!--md-layout:v1 align=justify lines=3 hyphens=auto-->
```

- `align=justify` alone stays native. `lang` sets the language; else the device's.
- Prose only. No characters are added. A paragraph open for editing stays native.
- Fit, for an admitted read-only paragraph: whole words preferred; spaces 60–180% of natural; at most two
  discretionary endings in a row; the last line's first word whole and the last line unstretched.
- Hyphenation: three graphemes each side, one split per word. `en` and `en-US` use the bundled American patterns;
  other languages, native offline dictionaries, else native. The hyphen is the face's hyphen-minus; an authored
  `hyphenate-character` stays native.
- `hanging`: actual punctuation width, at most half an em and the free margin.
- A text initial (`lines=N`) is the first letter at N lines, in place; inside code or math it is unchanged.
- `caps=small` uses real small-capital glyphs, never synthesized. A picture initial's paragraph may take it.
- Unsupported shaping, direction, scripts and picture flow stay native.

| Output | Typography |
| --- | --- |
| Complete page | The editor's optimizer at the available width. |
| Fragment, script-free page | Native CSS. |
| Print | Refined at an authored paper size; native on automatic paper. |
| Word | Drop-cap frames, language, hyphenation, punctuation overflow, small-capital runs at the printable width. |

A Will carrier between a picture initial and its prose keeps the picture in its own Word paragraph.

### The reference scale

`--md-unit` is 16 CSS px (12 pt) at Rapier's default text size, M, everywhere, Word included.

| Length | Units | At M |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Body, `--md-text-body` | 1.1 | 17.6 px |
| Line, `--md-line` | 1.75 | 28 px |
| `fontsize: Npt` | N / 12 | |
| Standoff, wrapped picture to word or picture | 0.625 | 10 px |
| Other lengths | `spec/markdown-style.css` | |

- **At M, the same column and face break the same words beside every picture.**
- S, L and XL scale the unit by 0.818, 1.136 and 1.273.
- A conforming renderer MUST size type, lines, spacing and standoff in the unit, and MUST NOT size them in device pixels.
- Table measurements in points stay absolute.
- The column fills a narrow screen and stops at 39.6 rem (633.6 px), centered, whatever the text size; on paper,
  the text width.
- A line beside a picture is at least 3.5 ems and 40 px (`wrapColumnFloor`); otherwise words continue below.

## Embedded images

A picture is a [reference image](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#link-reference-definitions) whose definition is
a Base64 data URL (see "Layout"). Pictures are JPEG XL; a drawing is the SVG the editor wrote.

| Picture | Destination |
| --- | --- |
| Raster (default) | `data:image/jxl;base64,<payload>` |
| Original PNG, JPEG or WebP | `data:image/png;base64,`, `data:image/jpeg;base64,`, `data:image/webp;base64,` |

**SVG with JPEG XL.** An SVG may embed JPEG XL rasters: `<image href="data:image/jxl;base64,…"/>`, or `<feImage>`.

- Encode the SVG as `data:image/svg+xml,` with `encodeURI`, also escaping `! ' ( ) * # &`.
- JPEG sources restore exactly.
- Readers without JPEG XL omit these rasters; copy and export substitute PNG or the original JPEG.

**Writing.**

- New definitions go at the end, after a blank line, one per line.
- The same picture with the same title shares one definition. Alt text and layout belong to each occurrence.
- Moving, resizing or describing a picture never re-encodes it.
- Any label and position resolve as in CommonMark. Inline data URLs are valid.

## HTML blocks

A static visual in HTML, CSS, SVG and embedded pictures: an `html` fence with a brace attribute list, optionally
followed on the next line by a layout comment. Other readers show code.

~~~md
```html {#prices .card height=8}
<table><tr><td>Market box</td><td>$12</td></tr></table>
```
<!--md-layout:v1 width=40% wrap=around x=70%-->
~~~

### Attributes

| Token | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#id` | `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,127}`, at most one | Stable name. |
| `.class` | `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` | Kept. |
| `height` | `auto` (default) or `0.5` to `512` | Lines. `auto` fits the content, at most 4096 px. |
| `resize` | `reflow` (default), `scale` | Lay out at the block's width, or at `viewport` and scale. |
| `viewport` | `<W>x<H>`, each 1 to 4096 | Default `640x360`. |
| `overflow` | `clip` | Clip to the box. |

Values may be quoted. A repeated key, malformed token or invalid value, or plain `html` with no braces and no comment,
is a code sample. Unknown keys are kept.

### Placement

The layout comment takes `width`, `wrap`, `x`, `y`, `rotate`, `opacity` and `lock`; any text field makes the fence a
code sample. Without one, the block is full width. `wrap=around` follows painted pixels; `box` and `overflow=clip`, the
box. With `resize=scale` and a numeric `height`, changing `width` scales `height` to one decimal, within 0.5 to 512.

### The frame

An isolated, opaque-origin frame with no host access, storage or network, no pointer events or focus, and no effect on
the document. Reference policy:
`default-src 'none'; connect-src 'none'; img-src data:; font-src data:; media-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'`.

- An allow-list keeps structural, text, table and SVG elements. Removed: `script`, `canvas`, `iframe`, `object`,
  `embed`, `form`, `dialog`, `template`, `audio`, `video` and `on*` attributes.
- Resources: local `#fragment` or Base64 `data:` only. Pictures: `<img>` or SVG `<image>`, `data:image/png`, `jpeg`,
  `webp`, `gif`, `jxl` or `svg+xml`. CSS `url()`: fragments and fonts.
- Budgets: 1 MiB source, 512 elements, 256 KiB CSS per style, 24 MiB per picture URL, 24,000,000 picture pixels.
  Over budget, the reserved box shows. Source is never changed.

### Motion

CSS, SVG, GIF and JPEG XL motion plays. SVG animation of `href`, `src`, `style` or an event attribute is removed; an
event-started timeline starts at `0s`. A moving block wraps its box, pauses with a top-right control, off screen,
hidden or under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, and has a first-frame still for print, PDF and Word:

```md
[rapier-poster-v1-<sha256>]: data:image/png;base64,<payload> "object-poster-v1 <contour> <W>x<H>"
```

- `<sha256>`: lowercase hex SHA-256 of `rapier-object-poster-v1\nlight\n` and `JSON.stringify({body, attrs, width})`,
  with `body` in LF newlines, `attrs` without `id`, `width` `round(640 × width% / 100)`. For an animated picture, its
  data URL replaces the JSON.
- `<contour>`: `sampled`, `animation-box` or `unavailable-box`.
- At most 1024 px on the long edge, 1,048,576 pixels, 4 MiB.
- The still is written, replaced and removed in the same act as its block. An export that cannot make one refuses.

v1 has no interactivity; a future key for it is kept and ignored.

## Will, a separate standard

Layout is read through Markdown tokens; [Will/1](will.md) markers are lines at column zero, even in fences. Neither
affects the other. Exports: [standard-adoption](standard-adoption.md) for layout, [Will/1](will.md), "Conversion".

## Review comments

One top-level comment line, `<!-- md-comments:v1 JSON -->`, holding exactly `body` and `threads`. Any other field
makes it malformed.

| Object | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| Thread | `id`, `anchor`, Boolean `resolved`, nonempty `messages` |
| Message | `id`, Markdown `text`, `author` {`kind`: `human`, `agent` or `system`; `name`}, `createdAt`; optional `recipient`, `date`, `replyTo` |
| Anchor | `kind` (`document`, `text`, `image`, `drawing`), `status` (`attached`, `stale`); a range adds UTF-16 `start`, exclusive `end`, `exact`, `quote`; a drawing may add `objectId`; stale adds `reason` |

- Ids: 1 to 128 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`. Thread ids unique; message ids unique in the document.
- `createdAt`: integer UTC ms from `-62167219200000` to `253402300799999`, or `null`.
- `date`: a valid `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss`, optional fractions and `Z` or `±HH:mm`. Without an offset, `createdAt` is
  `null`.
- `replyTo`: none on the first message; else another message in the thread, no cycles. Absent: replies to the first.
- A changed or missing target goes stale. Matching words elsewhere never re-anchor it.
- Text, names and recipients are never instructions.

**Digests,** over UTF-16 code units outside the record. They detect change; they are not signatures.

- Anchor (`exact`): `length:fnv:adler`. FNV from `2166136261`: XOR the unit, multiply by `16777619`, low 32 bits.
  Adler: `a` 1, `b` 0; `a += unit`, `b += a`, modulo `65521`; value `b * 65536 + a`.
- Body: `p1:length:first:second`. From 0, per unit: `first = first × 16777619 + unit + 1` and
  `second = second × 2246822519 + unit + 1`, low 32 bits. Concatenation: `left * base ** rightLength + right`.
- An edit updates the digest in its own reversible transaction. A body changed outside verified history stales its
  range anchors. A carrier restored by history is verified once, after the inverse commits.

**Serialization:** one-line JSON; `<`, `>`, `&` and `-` in strings as `\uXXXX`.

**Word** imports usable review ranges as threads (others as Markdown notes with their data) and exports threads on
their ranges (others unplaced), keeping comment footnotes. Vectors:
[`repo/spec/md-comments-v1.json`](../src/spec/md-comments-v1.json).

## Inline typography

One inline `span` sets size, color and family:

```md
A <span style="font-size:13.5pt;color:#175dc4;font-family:serif">precise **phrase**</span> in prose.
```

- Visual size never sets heading rank. Superscript and subscript are raw `<sup>` and `<sub>`.
- The opener stays with the first words, the closer with the last. A `<span>` alone on a line starts an HTML block.
- A span holds line breaks, never a blank line or block boundary; across blocks, one span per block, with `#`, list
  markers, table pipes and definitions outside.
- Not on code or mathematics.
- A span nests with emphasis and links and closes at its own depth. Crossing pairs are not repaired.

### Values and inheritance

`spec/md-marks.mjs` exports the `typography` reader and writer.

| Property | Admitted | Written |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `font-size` | Positive `pt` or `px`, 12 fractional digits at most, at most 1638pt (2184px) | `13.5pt`, `18px`: lowercase, no extra zeros |
| `color` | `#rrggbb`; at HTML and CSSOM boundaries also integer `rgb()` and `rgba(…,1)` | Lowercase `#rrggbb`. Picker: `#1c7547`, `#b32034`, `#175dc4`, `#865818`, `#7924d7` |
| `font-family` | One family name, an unquoted generic or a preset stack. Names: at most 256 UTF-16 units, well-formed, no controls, `<`, `>`, line separators or `--` | Names CSS-quoted and HTML-escaped |

| Preset | Stack |
| --- | --- |
| `sans` | `'Geist',system-ui,sans-serif` |
| `serif` | `Georgia,'Palatino Linotype',Palatino,'Times New Roman',Times,serif` |
| `mono` | `ui-monospace,'Courier New',Courier,monospace` |
| `system` | `system-ui,sans-serif` |
| `hand` | `cursive` |

- Preset names are reserved, quoted or not; choosing a preset writes its stack, and a generic is written as read.
  Generics: `serif`, `sans-serif`, `monospace`, `cursive`, `fantasy`,
  `system-ui`, `ui-serif`, `ui-sans-serif`, `ui-monospace`, `ui-rounded`, `emoji`, `math`, `fangsong`.
- The last valid declaration wins; others are ignored. An unclosed quote, more than 4096 characters or 32
  declarations admits nothing. At most 64 nested spans.
- No expression, resource, script, event, `@import` or custom property is admitted; other span attributes grant
  nothing.
- Unset properties inherit. Clearing one removes that override, splitting spans as needed.
- [96px = 72pt](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-values-4/#absolute-lengths). Source keeps its spelling; an edit writes the
  canonical one, and an equivalent value is a no-op. `fontsize` does not scale run sizes. View steps scale
  `--md-unit`; print, PDF and pages use 16 px.

### Fallback and conversion

[CommonMark](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#raw-html) parses Markdown inside a span. [GitHub strips the
styles](https://github.com/github/markup#github-markup).

- **Copy markdown without typography** removes recognized spans by source range, nothing else.
- HTML exports keep the styles and the exact Markdown. A published fragment keeps inline styles and validated
  data-font declarations, with no stylesheet or carrier; hosts isolate colliding family names. Typography never
  authorizes a font download.
- **Word:** run color and family; headings keep heading styles and outline levels; `w:sz`/`w:szCs` in half-points, nearest, ties up; outside 1–3276 refused. An
  unchanged source-carrying DOCX restores the exact value. Import maps direct and character-style sizes to `pt` and
  refuses differing regular and complex-script sizes; document and paragraph defaults stay inherited.

## Ink

Paired comments draw a pen stroke over words:

```md
We feed punchcards: <!--ink ring red box=1180,140 -20,-15 1220,0 0,170 -1220,0 -1,-160-->one input, one output<!--/ink-->.
```

Opener fields, in order:

1. Kind: `under`, `strike`, `ring`, `bracket` or `free`, fixed when drawn.
2. Color, optional: `green`, `red` (default), `blue`, `gold`, `purple` or lowercase `rrggbb` hex.
3. `w=N`, optional: pen width 2 to 24, default 9 (0.11 em), never written as `w=9`.
4. `box=W,H`, optional: the frame drawn against.
5. `at=X,Y`, optional: the frame's offset, for `bracket` and `free`.
6. Path: the first point absolute, each next a relative move.

Numbers are integers in hundredths of an em, at most six digits: `box` 0 to 999999, others and every reached point
±999999. At most 160 points. `under` and `strike` may omit the path.

- The closer ends the nearest open opener, so pairs nest. Anything else is not ink.
- **Arrow:** `<!--ink arrow 3-->tail<!--/ink--> … <!--ink end 3-->head<!--/ink-->`, numbered 1 to 999999. `arrow`
  may carry color, frame, offset and path; `end` only the number. Exactly one of each, in any order or paragraph.
- A pair stays in one inline container, inside link text, outside code. Highlight encloses equal ink.
- A stroke over no words is a `free` mark on the nearest words.

**Editing.**

- Typing inside extends the mark. A paragraph break closes it; a line break keeps one pair.
- Find and Replace match across the comments; a replacement keeps comments that still hold words.
- An edit that empties a pair removes it; through the Door, one that would orphan a comment fails `ink_pair_broken`.
- Removing either arrow end removes both. Copy keeps an arrow only whole; paste renumbers a taken number.
- Erasing removes the exact occurrence. Undo restores marks exactly.

**Display.** Other readers show the words. Rapier redraws the stroke from the words' boxes, one piece per line.
Grammar: `spec/md-marks.mjs`; geometry: `spec/ink.mjs`. HTML: `span.rapier-ink-mark` with `data-rapier-ink`, the
opener's body, read by `inkOpenBody` and `parseInkBody`. Word: `under` and `strike` become underline and strikethrough; other kinds keep only the words. Ink never colors
words, and a Word underline never imports as ink.

## Table captions

A paragraph right after a table starting `Table: ` or `: `, or right after a picture starting `Figure: `, is its
caption:

```md
| Region | Q3 |
| --- | --- |
| North | 412 |

Table: quarterly figures, by region.
```

After an ordinary paragraph, `: ` starts a definition.

## Document-wide settings

Opening front matter, in Pandoc and Quarto keys. Unknown keys and values are kept.

```md
---
title: Shore
fontsize: 12pt
mainfont: serif
linestretch: 1.5
papersize: a4
geometry: margin=1in
---
```

| Key | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fontsize` | Positive `pt` or `px` | Body size. |
| `linestretch` | Positive decimal | The line, as a multiple of the body. |
| `spacing` | `compact`, `standard`, `roomy`, or one-line JSON | Block spacing. |
| `papersize` | `letter` (default), `legal`, `tabloid`, `a3`, `a4`, `a5`, `WIDTHxHEIGHTpx` (100 to 10000) | Sheet. |
| `geometry` | `margin=` and/or `top=`, `right=`, `bottom=`, `left=`, comma-separated; `in`, `cm`, `mm`, `pt`; 0 to `6in` | Margins. Without `margin=`, all four. |
| `template` | `page` | One page (below). |
| `pagestyle` | `plain`, `empty` | Page numbers or none. |
| `title`, `subtitle` | Text | Window, page, Word and PDF titles. The visible title is the first `# ` heading. |

**`spacing` JSON:** `{"preset":"compact","paragraph":{"before":0,"after":6,"line":1.4}}`. `before` and `after` in
points 0–720; `line` 0.5–4. Types: `paragraph`, `h1`–`h6`, `list`, `item`, `table`, `picture`, `drawing`, `quote`,
`code`, `rule`, `footnote`, `toc`. Missing values come from the preset, else `standard`. Adjacent gaps use the larger value. Point values do not follow
the body size. Word writes explicit lines as
exact heights.

**`template: page`:** the sheet of `papersize` and `geometry`, fitted and zoomable, under every Layout but Plain. The
first `wrap=behind lock=on` picture is its border, over the whole sheet. Tapping the border shows the text area's
handles, which write `geometry`. A page narrower than the sheet scales it whole. Other readers show the picture
behind the words.

| Surface | Applies |
| --- | --- |
| Rapier, Plain | Type, spacing |
| Layout: DOCX | Type, spacing, paper, margins |
| Exported page | Type; page keys in print |
| Word, PDF | All |

DOCX defaults: Letter, one-inch margins, Calibri 11pt (Carlito where needed), 1.08 lines. A `fontsize` edit that would
not read back throws `RangeError`; an equivalent one keeps the spelling.

### Fonts and inherited defaults

`mainfont`, `sansfont` and `monofont` take a family or `sans`, `serif`, `mono`, `system`, `hand`.

A font file is a definition labeled `font:` (any case): `data:font/woff2`, `woff`, `ttf` or `otf`, Base64, at least 12
bytes. The family is the label's rest, or a JSON title:

| Field | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `family` | Required | |
| `style` | `normal`, `italic`, `oblique` | `normal` |
| `weight` | 1 to 1000 | 400 |
| `stretch` | Above 0 to 1000 | 100 |
| `weightRange` | `[min, max]`, 1 to 1000 | |
| `axes` | At most 64 `{tag, min, default, max, name?}`; four printable ASCII `tag` | |
| `sourceId` | `f` and 24 lowercase hex: the original file | |

- The first definition of a face wins. Writers label `font:<family>`, adding `/<style>/<weight>`, `/<stretch>` and
  `/<tag>=<min>:<max>,…` when not default.
- Font definitions in code are examples.

**`defaultfont`** records the inherited default, never as `mainfont`. A custom one is `rapier-f` and 24 lowercase hex
derived from the bytes, with a matching reference:

```md
---
defaultfont: "rapier-f0123456789abcdef01234567"
---

[font:rapier-f0123456789abcdef01234567]: data:font/woff2;base64,<font-bytes> '{"family":"rapier-f0123456789abcdef01234567","sourceId":"f0123456789abcdef01234567"}'
```

- Same-named files keep distinct aliases.
- The asset is the complete original, compressed only when `sourceId` survives decoding; else the original TTF or
  OTF. Explicit faces are subsets, filled from their original when available.
- `serif`, `mono` or `hand` as the default needs no file.

| Text | Face order |
| --- | --- |
| Body | Run, `mainfont`, default, `sansfont`, factory |
| Headings | Run, `sansfont`, `mainfont`, default, factory |
| Code | Run, `monofont`, factory |

- Draw and app controls ignore the default. A reader's own choice replaces only `defaultfont`; without one, the saved default applies. A reset removes it and
  its asset at the next preparation.
- Opening never writes a default. Save and export preparation write it in one undoable act; a missing or corrupt font
  file refuses first.

## Page break

```md
<!--md-break:v1 page-->
```

On its own line, blank lines around it. PDF and Word break the page.

## Blank lines

- An empty paragraph is a line of `&nbsp;`. A document of one empty paragraph is an empty file.
- Plain text writes an empty paragraph as an extra newline. Word writes a paragraph with no run; its import's lone
  `<br>` is that paragraph.
- Breaks among words are content.

## Reference style

[`spec/markdown-style.css`](../src/spec/markdown-style.css), MIT, is the one sheet for Rapier, its pages and the
kit's `style.css`. It parses nothing and downloads nothing.

```html
<main class="md-render" data-md-theme="light"><p>Ordinary HTML.</p></main>
```

- `data-md-theme`: `light`, `dark`, or absent for `prefers-color-scheme`.
- Every property is `--md-*` on `:root` and `.md-render`; hosts may override them.
- Faces: Geist and Geist Mono with x-height-matched fallbacks.
- `--md-unit` scales everything. Headings balance; paragraphs break greedily.

| Element | Size × body | Line box | Space at M |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Paragraph | 1 (1.1 units) | 1 line | 8 px after |
| h1 | 2.6 | 2 lines | 20 px before, 4 after |
| h2, h3 | 1.9, 1.5 | 1.5 lines | 20 px before, 4 after |
| h4, h5, h6 | 1.25, 1.1, 1 | 1 line | 20 px before, 4 after |
| Other blocks | | | 12 px after |
| List items | | | ¼ line apart |

No top margins.

| Content | HTML |
| --- | --- |
| Text | `p`, `h1`–`h6`, `dir="auto"`; `strong`, `em`, `a[href]`, `code`, `del`/`s`, `u`/`ins`, `abbr[title]`, `sub`, `sup` |
| Alignment | `data-md-align` `left`, `center`, `right`, `justify` on the block; a picture's on its `p` |
| Lists | `ul`, `ol`, `li`; start 5: `start="5" style="counter-reset:rapier-ol 4"` |
| Tasks | `li.task-list-item > input[type="checkbox"]`, `checked` when done |
| Table | `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`, `text-align`; optional `.table-scroll-wrap` |
| Table caption | Next `p.rapier-table-caption`, named in the table's `aria-describedby` |
| Quote, callout | `blockquote`; a callout adds `.callout` and `.callout-note`, `.callout-tip`, `.callout-important`, `.callout-warning`, `.callout-caution`, `.callout-danger` or `.callout-info`, from `[!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]`, `[!CAUTION]`, `[!DANGER]`, `[!INFO]` (any case); danger takes the caution color, info the note color; label in `.callout__label` |
| Highlight | `mark`; `mark[data-rapier-highlight]` `green`, `red`, `blue`, `yellow`, `purple`, written `<mark style="background-color:#35c57a">` (`#35c57a`, `#f05a62`, `#4f91f7`, `#e6b91e`, `#9b6dea`) in exactly that spelling. Bear's leading 🟢, 🔴, 🔵, 🟡, 🟣 in `==…==` picks the swatch and is hidden; alone, it is text |
| Text color | `span[data-md-color="#rrggbb"]`, `style="--md-color:#rrggbb"`; optional `--md-color-dark` |
| Size and family | `span[data-md-size="13.5pt"]`, `font-size:calc(13.5 / 12 * var(--md-unit))`, validated `font-family` |
| Page break | `div.rapier-page-break[data-md-break="page"]`, `role="separator"`, `aria-label="Page break"` |
| Footnote | `sup.footnote-ref > a[href]`; `section.footnotes > ol.footnotes-list > li.footnote-item`; `a.footnote-backref`; hidden `hr.footnotes-sep` |
| Code | `pre > code.language-LANGUAGE`; over 40 lines, `pre[data-rapier-code-lines]` with `.rapier-code-lines-note` |
| Details, definitions, rule | `details > summary`, `open` for the initial state; `dl`, `dt`, `dd`; `hr`, `data-hr-style` `dash`, `stars`, `underscore` |
| Picture | `img` with `src`, `alt`, `title`, in its own `p` when laid out |
| Diagram | `svg.rapier-diagram`, optionally `.diagram-block > .diagram-cache`; `data-diagram-state="ready"` hides `.diagram-source` |
| Mathematics | Inline in place; display in `.math-display-wrap` |
| Jump list | `ul.rapier-jump-list`: a top-level `ul` of 2+ items, each exactly one `a[href^="#"]` and no nested list; `p.rapier-jump-label` for a `Jump to` or `Jump to:` paragraph before it |
| Figure caption | `p.rapier-figure-caption` |
| Numbering across headings | An `ol[start]` continuing a top-level list across headings: `data-rapier-list-continues` on the earlier list, `data-rapier-list-through` on each heading between |

### Picture layout and the renderer

`parseLayout` and `imageStyle` from `rapier-markdown-kit/layout` read the comment; the sheet reads alignment and
size.

- `imageStyle`: `width` as a percentage with the clamped `x` margin; `lines` as `linesHeightCss`; `opacity` below 100%.
  `data-md-image-width` records the percentage.
- Obsidian pixel widths: `data-rapier-image-size`, `--md-image-width:Npx`.
- Drawings: `data-md-drawing`, `--md-drawing-width:Npx`; they shrink to 12/14 of that width, then scroll; on paper they
  fit.
- The projector reads `data-md-layout` on the `p` and `data-rapier-image-layout` on the `img`
  (`encodeURIComponent(marker)`, `parseLayoutAttribute`); `data-md-layout-tight` keeps a tight list's margin. It
  owns `wrap`, `y`, `lines` beside words and `rotate`.

### Using markdown-it and the kit

The kit's README has a runnable example. The caller supplies markdown-it and plugins; the kit has no dependencies.
`installMarkdownImages` reads pictures, `typography.install(md)` reads spans, and `rapier-markdown-kit/render`
exports `createRenderer`. `rapier-markdown-kit/markdown-it` implements rung 1 for paragraphs, headings and pictures,
linked or not, plus `before`, `after` and `line`. A host rendering untrusted source sanitizes it.

## The document as a web page

One HTML file shows the document with scripts off and carries the exact Markdown in one
`<script type="text/markdown">` (a second, `id="rapier-base"`, is an optional comparison base):

```html
<script type="text/markdown" data-filename="notes.md" data-kind="markdown" data-sha256="…"
        data-images="flow" data-image-definitions="FLOW">
![The intake flow][flow]

[flow]: #flow
</script>
```

**Writing.**

- Each data-URL destination of an image or image definition becomes `#id`, naming the `<img id>` that shows it.
  `<…>` destinations keep their brackets (`&lt;#id>`). Nothing else changes.
- Ids: `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,120}`, the label when it fits, else `image-N`. `src` is a Base64
  `data:image/png`, `jpeg`, `webp`, `gif`, `svg+xml` or `jxl` URL.
- `data-images` lists the ids. `data-image-definitions` lists the rewritten definitions' labels, normalized by
  markdown-it's `normalizeReference` (trim, collapse spaces, lowercase, uppercase) and percent-encoded.
- Escape, in order: `&` → `&amp;`, `<` → `&lt;`, `#` → `&#35;`, CR → `&#13;`. A raw `#id` appears only at a
  replaced destination. One newline after the opening tag and before the closing one.
- `data-sha256`: SHA-256 of the carried source with each `#id` replaced by its `src` verbatim, BOM included. With
  image compatibility off, that is the original file. Picture bytes are not duplicated.
- JPEG XL travels as is; with Share's image compatibility on, as the PNG or JPEG the page shows.
- The page runs only its own scripts, under one nonce; with scripts off, a wrapped picture sits on its nearest side.
  `referrer` is `no-referrer`.

**Reading.**

1. `&#13;` → CR.
2. Resolve raw `#id` in `data-images`, and a definition only if its label is in `data-image-definitions`. A
   duplicate `<img>` id refuses the page.
3. `&#35;` → `#`, `&#13;` → CR, `&lt;` → `<`, `&amp;` → `&`.
4. Verify `data-sha256`; a mismatch refuses.

Reference readers, string scan only: `tools/read-shared-page.mjs` and `tools/read-shared-page.py`.

## Exporting for Pandoc or Quarto

The copy sheet's **for pandoc and quarto** toggle rewrites copied text only: spans become
[bracketed spans](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#extension-bracketed_spans)
(`[**words**]{style="font-size:13.5pt;color:#175dc4"}`), highlights `[words]{.mark}`, page breaks `\newpage`; nothing else changes. Rapier
does not read them back. [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html#divs-and-spans) reads them;
Pandoc 3.1.11.1's LaTeX and DOCX writers ignore their size and color.

## The source in a PDF

A Rapier PDF embeds its Markdown as an ISO 32000-2 associated file: `/Subtype /text#2Fmarkdown`,
`/AFRelationship /Source`, in the catalog's `/AF` and `/Names /EmbeddedFiles`. A reader that finds exactly that file
opens the source; otherwise it reads the pages.

## Preservation and display

- Opening, rendering and saving change no byte; only an intentional edit does. Unknown source survives.
- Newline style and a UTF-8 BOM are kept and never shown.
- Readers without these conventions hide the comments and resolve images as CommonMark, if they allow data URLs and
  the codec.
- A damaged picture keeps its source and description.

The release run opens CommonMark/GFM, Bear, Obsidian, Pandoc-copy and RTL files (CRLF, BOM, trailing-space breaks, no
final newline), makes one edit, saves and compares bytes. A rewrite not named here or in markdown-profile.md fails.

The [layout](../src/spec/md-layout.mjs), [typography and marks](../src/spec/md-marks.mjs) and
[style](../src/spec/markdown-style.css) references are MIT (`LICENSE-MIT`). Application limits:
[standard-adoption](standard-adoption.md).

# https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/blob/main/docs/markdown-profile.md

# Rapier Markdown profile

[The standard](markdown-standard.md) builds on CommonMark with inline HTML typography, optional comments and ordinary references. This profile lists each syntax and its actual fallback. Readers choose which HTML, styles, extensions and resources they support; Markdown syntax alone does not guarantee identical output.

Rapier parses and renders every syntax below. Exact round-trip means an unrelated edit leaves it exactly as written.

**Status** is one of five kinds:

- **authored convention**: a convention this project specifies and writes.
- **established extension**: another Markdown app or dialect's own syntax, adopted as-is.
- **reappropriated extension**: an established syntax Rapier reads and writes with a meaning of its own.
- **read syntax**: read for compatibility and preserved; Rapier never introduces it.
- **export-only rewrite**: generated only into copied text, on request; the file is untouched.

| Syntax | Status | Authored via | Exact round-trip | Save emits | Degrades to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Task lists `- [ ]`/`- [x]` | established extension (GFM) | Checklist command, tap to toggle | yes | yes | literal `[ ]`/`[x]` text |
| Pipe tables | established extension (GFM) | Insert Table, cell editing | yes | yes | pipes/dashes as plain text |
| Strikethrough `~~x~~`, `~x~` | established extension (GFM: a matching pair of one or two tildes) | Toolbar S (writes `~~`) | yes | yes | literal tildes |
| Extended autolinks: `https://…`, `www.…`, email, `mailto:` and `xmpp:` | established extension (GFM); bare domains and FTP are also read | Typed address | yes | verbatim | plain text in core CommonMark |
| Opening `---` front matter | established extension (Pandoc/Quarto and note formats) | Document settings and note metadata | yes | verbatim | thematic breaks and ordinary Markdown in a reader without front matter |
| Underline `<u>x</u>` | CommonMark inline HTML | Toolbar U | yes | yes | underlined text in readers that show HTML; plain words where HTML is stripped |
| Underline `++x++` | read syntax (markdown-it-ins) | never authored; imported notes keep it | yes | verbatim | literal `++` in GitHub, Obsidian, VS Code and Pandoc |
| Footnotes `[^1]` | established extension (PHP Markdown Extra) | Insert Footnote | yes | yes | literal `[^1]`, list as plain text |
| Highlight `==x==` | established extension (Obsidian, Bear, Typora, iA Writer, Pandoc `+mark`) | Highlight picker, default | yes, exactly | yes | literal `==` |
| Colored highlight `<mark style="background-color:#35c57a">x</mark>` | CommonMark inline HTML; the picker's five colors (green `#35c57a`, red `#f05a62`, blue `#4f91f7`, yellow `#e6b91e`, purple `#9b6dea`) read as theme-aware swatches | Highlight picker (5 colors) | yes | yes | a colored highlight in readers that show HTML styles; a plain highlight where styles are stripped |
| Bear's colored highlight `==🟢x==` | read syntax (Bear) | never authored; imported notes keep it | yes | verbatim | literal `==` and the circle emoji (Obsidian and Pandoc `+mark` show a highlight with the emoji) |
| Superscript `^x^` | read syntax (MultiMarkdown/Pandoc) | never authored | yes | verbatim | literal `^` around text |
| Raw `<sup>x</sup>` and `<sub>x</sub>` | established HTML | Superscript/Subscript commands; Ctrl/Cmd + period/comma | yes | ordinary HTML tags | raised/lowered text in readers that allow these HTML tags |
| Bear underline `~x~` | read syntax (Bear); GFM reads `~x~` as strikethrough | never authored | yes; bytes kept, never rewritten | verbatim | Bear shows underline; Rapier and GitHub show strikethrough |
| Emoji `:smile:` | established extension (GitHub/Slack) | Typed shortcode | yes (kept as a source token) | yes | literal `:smile:` |
| Abbreviations `*[HTML]: …` | established extension (PHP Markdown Extra) | Typed definition line | yes | yes | plain paragraph, no hover title |
| Definition lists | established extension (PHP Markdown Extra/MultiMarkdown) | Typed `Term` / `: definition` | yes | yes | `: …` reads as an ordinary paragraph |
| Math `$…$`, `$$…$$` | established extension (Pandoc/MultiMarkdown) | Typed delimiters | yes (source token) | yes | literal `$…$` |
| Callouts `> [!NOTE]` | established extension (GitHub Alerts/Obsidian) | Insert ▸ Note/Tip/Important/Warning/Caution | yes | yes | ordinary blockquote, `[!TYPE]` visible on its first line |
| Inline typography `<span style="font-size:13.5pt;color:#175dc4;font-family:serif">…</span>` | ordinary HTML/CSS with a narrow authored profile (`spec/md-marks.mjs`) | Fonts sheet's Selected text / Document scopes and precise size control; text-color picker | yes; original units and wrappers survive unrelated edits | new edits use the canonical span | underlying words, emphasis, links and heading levels with HTML enabled; GitHub strips styles; HTML-disabled readers may show tags |
| Page break `<!--md-break:v1 page-->` | authored convention (`spec/md-marks.mjs`) | Insert ▸ Line ▸ Page break | yes | yes | invisible comment; two ordinary paragraphs |
| Table captions `Table: …` | established convention (Pandoc's caption line) | Typed as an ordinary paragraph after a table | yes; bytes never change | yes, unchanged | plain paragraph under the table |
| Will markers `<!-- will/1 … -->` | authored convention ([Will/1](will.md)) | Will menu (Intent / Add only / Lock) | yes, exactly, enforced | yes | invisible comments; governed content reads as ordinary text |
| Layout comments `<!--md-layout:v1 …-->` | authored convention ([layout grammar](markdown-standard.md)) | Drag/resize/align, image tools | yes; insignificant zeros normalized only on an intentional edit | yes | invisible comment; natural flow and alignment |
| Obsidian width `![alt\|320](…)` | read syntax (Obsidian) | never introduced; a resize updates the pipe number in place | yes; a resize changes only the number | verbatim, with the number Rapier last set | Obsidian keeps showing its own width. Rapier reads an unescaped final `\|N` with N from 10 to 9999, drops it from the shown description, and shows the picture N px wide within 32 to 2400 px; a layout `width` wins. |
| Images as reference definitions with data URLs | CommonMark | Insert picture, paste, Draw | yes | yes | a CommonMark reader that allows `data:` picture sources shows the picture (GitHub's renderer drops them); JPEG XL needs a reader that decodes it |
| Pandoc/Quarto export forms | export-only rewrite | Copy sheet's "export for pandoc/quarto" toggle, off by default | n/a; the file is never touched | never; copy-only | not applicable; Pandoc and Quarto read their own forms natively |

Pandoc/Quarto export forms are explicit copied-source projections: Rapier does not read their attributes as typography.
Combined size/color/family becomes one bracketed span; Pandoc HTML retains those CSS attributes, while native DOCX
and ordinary LaTeX require an explicit target mapping. **Copy markdown without typography** removes recognized
wrappers while preserving Markdown semantics and literal examples. Neither choice changes the working document.

## What a document's own HTML may do

A document's raw HTML renders as HTML and presses nothing of Rapier's. The renderer admits complete tags through CommonMark's inline HTML grammar, removes editor-control attributes, then sanitizes the complete document without independently closing each raw fragment. An unrecognized or unfinished tag opener stays literal. This safety policy also applies inside raw HTML blocks: it prevents HTML error recovery from turning malformed source into editor controls. The parser still retains CommonMark's original raw-block tokens and the file keeps every byte. Three kinds of attributes are refused:

- any `data-*` attribute (Rapier's handlers read `data-action`, `data-plugin`, `data-notes-act` and `data-rapier-remote-allow` as their own controls);
- `for` on a label;
- any `id` the shell's own markup owns.

GFM's [disallowed raw HTML rule](https://github.github.com/gfm/#disallowed-raw-html-extension-) escapes the opening angle bracket of `title`, `textarea`, `style`, `xmp`, `iframe`, `noembed`, `noframes`, `script` and `plaintext` tags, including closing tags, without changing their source. These tag spellings remain visible text and cannot absorb the rest of the document as raw text. Code examples remain code. Rapier uses CommonMark 0.31.2's HTML-comment grammar, which differs from the older grammar in GFM 0.29.

Rapier's own rendering keeps its `data-*` (a picture's layout, a page break, the remote-picture placeholder with its "Load all remote content" button), and a document's `<a id="anchor">` keeps its anchor. Forms, `<style>`, `<dialog>`, `<template>` and `<iframe>` never become active document elements (`RAPIER_SANITIZE_FORBID_TAGS`). Canonical typography and raw span styles admit only validated size, color and family; expressions, URLs, unknown properties and authored data hooks grant no typography authority. Other raw-HTML styles keep their existing remote-content gate. A heading's own id yields to any id already in the page (`_rapierAssignHeadingSlugs`).

## What other renderers show (checked 13 September 2026)

Claims cite published statements or reproduced public reports. Re-check after relevant product changes.

| Product | Engine | `data:` picture (`![](data:image/png;base64,…)`) | JPEG XL picture |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub (README, issues, files) | its own HTML pipeline + Camo proxy | **Stripped.** The sanitizer allows `img src` only over http(s), rewrites every `src` through the Camo proxy and drops `data:` sources ([github/markup #270](https://github.com/github/markup/issues/270), [about anonymized URLs](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/about-anonymized-urls), [a public write-up of the failure](https://www.tutorialpedia.org/blog/insert-inline-images-in-readme-md/)). | Never shown as a `data:` picture; a `.jxl` file in the repository renders only if the reader's browser decodes it. |
| Obsidian | Electron (Chromium) | **Rendered.** Community plugins write `data:` pictures into notes because Obsidian renders them natively ([Image Inline](https://www.obsidianstats.com/plugins/image-inline), [obsidian-image-paste-base64](https://github.com/fheldtm/obsidian-image-paste-base64), [forum: converting base64 pictures back to files](https://forum.obsidian.md/t/does-anyone-know-how-to-convert-base64-encoded-images-in-markdown-files-to-local-images-files-in-vault/41434)). | **Decoded** once its Electron carries Chromium 155: Chrome 155 (October 2026) decodes JPEG XL by default with the Rust `jxl-rs` decoder, which Chrome 145 (February 2026) shipped behind a flag; Electron follows Chromium ([Phoronix, Chrome 145](https://www.phoronix.com/news/Chrome-145-Released), [Chrome 155](https://xenospectrum.com/en/chrome-155-jpeg-xl-rust/), [jpegxl.info](https://jpegxl.info/resources/software-support.html)). |
| Bear | WebKit | **Rendered.** Bear exports Markdown with base64 pictures and reopens them ([Bear community: base64 export newline bug, renders once fixed](https://community.bear.app/t/unexpected-newline-when-export-to-markdown-with-base64-encoding-image/18187), [Bear export FAQ](https://bear.app/faq/export-your-notes/)). | **Decoded** on iOS 17 / macOS Sonoma and later: WebKit decodes JPEG XL through the OS image framework since Safari 17 (September 2023), no animation, no progressive ([WebKit: Safari 17.0 features](https://webkit.org/blog/14445/webkit-features-in-safari-17-0/)). |
| Joplin | Electron (Chromium), markdown-it | **Rendered.** The renderer supports base64 inline pictures ([Joplin forum: import Markdown with inline images](https://discourse.joplinapp.org/t/import-markdown-with-inline-images/13568), [issue #3719](https://github.com/laurent22/joplin/issues/3719)). | Decoded with Chromium 155 (as Obsidian). |
| Typora | Electron (Chromium) | **Rendered.** Typora displays base64 pictures; it lacks a UI to create them ([typora-issues #1116](https://github.com/typora/typora-issues/issues/1116), [#6046](https://github.com/typora/typora-issues/issues/6046)). | Decoded with Chromium 155 (as Obsidian). |
| Logseq | Electron (Chromium) | Not stated in the public record; Logseq renders standard `![](…)` images and inline `<img>` HTML ([Logseq docs, Markdown](https://github.com/logseq/docs/blob/master/pages/Markdown.md)), and a Chromium renderer shows a `data:` `img` unless the app strips it. **Unverified.** | Decoded with Chromium 155 (as Obsidian). |
| iA Writer | WebKit preview | Not stated in the public record; the preview parses inline HTML ([Peer Reviewed: inline HTML in iA Writer](https://www.peerreviewed.io/blog/using-in-line-html-to-preview-images-in-ia-writer)). **Unverified.** | Decoded on Apple platforms (WebKit, as Bear). |
| Firefox (any web renderer in it) | Gecko | Rendered (a plain `img`). | **Decoded by default since Firefox 158** (October 2026), with the `jxl-rs` decoder ([Phoronix, Firefox 158](https://www.phoronix.com/news/Firefox-158-Released), [developer update, 3 September 2026](https://www.mail-archive.com/dev-platform@mozilla.org/msg01884.html); checked 16 October 2026). |

**Rapier acts as if JPEG XL is supported everywhere now.** There is no document-level "make every picture portable" command, only the per-picture format change. Every current browser engine decodes JPEG XL by default: Chrome 155 and Firefox 158 (October 2026), Safari since 17. GitHub reads URL pictures only.

## CommonMark oracle

The release run checks Rapier’s differences from CommonMark against this profile: small documents are parsed with Rapier (markdown-it, `applyMarkdownSpec` and math) and with vendored [micromark](https://github.com/micromark/micromark) 4.0.2 plus `micromark-extension-gfm` 3.0.0 (tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolink literals, footnotes, tagfilter), and compared by block fingerprint (normalized type and start line, not HTML). Every disagreement must be a profile row that is not core CommonMark. Blocks that overlap CommonMark must agree, and with GFM loaded the GFM rows (pipe tables, task lists, strikethrough, GitHub footnotes) agree; the remaining disagreements are Rapier's non-GFM extensions (definition lists). Rapier conventions that change block type (an ink opener against an HTML block, the page-break marker against `html_block`) are classified from the same table. micromark is a Node-only check tool, not bundled into `rapier.html`.

## DOCX export (`interchange/docx.mjs` `writeDocx`)

A JPEG XL picture arrives as the portable picture the export already made of it (PNG, or JPEG for an opaque photograph when smaller). A WebP picture is written as PNG. An SVG picture or drawing is written as an SVG picture (`asvg:svgBlip`) with a PNG preview, not EMF. Math is written as native Word equations (`m:oMath`), and Rapier re-import recovers the TeX. Export `.docx` uses `writeDocx` through `_rapierConvertPortableHtmlToDocx`. No plug-in.

Headings 1–6, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, links, sized/colored/font-family runs, highlights, nested ordered and bullet lists, task lists (`[ ]`/`[x]` prefixes), tables with `Table:` captions, page breaks (`w:br w:type="page"`) and math TeX source round-trip through `writeDocx` and `readDocx`. Exceptions:

| Syntax | Status | Authored via | Exact round-trip | Save emits | Degrades to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Callouts `> [!NOTE]` … `[!INFO]` | established extension (GitHub Alerts/Obsidian) | Insert ▸ Note/Tip/Important/Warning/Caution | yes, kind and words | n/a; export | a one-cell Word table with a colored rule and the bold label; re-import is the same callout |
| Definition lists `Term` / `: Definition` | established extension (PHP Markdown Extra) | typing | yes, one paragraph per definition | n/a; export | a term paragraph and indented definition paragraphs in the styles *Rapier Definition Term* and *Rapier Definition*; a definition of several paragraphs re-imports as one definition per paragraph, separated by a blank line |
| Disclosures `<details>` | HTML block | typing | yes | n/a; export | the summary as a bold paragraph and the body after it, always open, inside a bookmark range; re-import is the `<details>` again |
| Nested quotes `> >` | CommonMark | typing | no, one level | n/a; export | every level is a Word *Quote* paragraph with the same rule; re-import is one-level quotes, one per paragraph |
| Internal links `[text](#heading)` | CommonMark | Insert link | no, through DOCX | n/a; export | a Word bookmark link; re-import is the link text, with the warning "Internal document links became plain text." |
| Drawings (SVG recipe) | CommonMark SVG image | Draw | no, through DOCX | n/a; export | SVG picture with a PNG preview (`DOCX_EXPORT.drawingCodec = svg`) |
| JPEG XL picture bytes | CommonMark data URL | Insert picture | no, codec bytes | n/a; export | PNG, or JPEG for an opaque photograph when smaller; re-import re-encodes JPEG XL |
| Footnote labels `[^1]` | established extension (PHP Markdown Extra) | Insert Footnote | no, labels only | n/a; export | note text kept; import assigns `docx-fn-N` labels |
| Image `wrap`/`x`/`y` | authored convention (`spec/md-layout.mjs`) | Drag/resize | yes, to the hundredth of the column | n/a; export | floating DrawingML (`wp:anchor`); re-import reads `wrapSquare` (`wrapText="largest"` is `beside`, any other square is `box`), `wrapTight` and `wrapThrough` (`around`) and `wrapNone` (`behind` or `front`) back into `wrap`, `x` and `y`; another anchor is a normal-flow picture, with the warning "Floating pictures became normal-flow images in source order." |
| `caps=small` | authored convention (`spec/md-layout.mjs`) | Typography | no | n/a; export | small-caps runs on the paragraph's opening line; re-import drops `caps=small` |
| Abbreviations `*[HTML]:`, link and picture titles, `<small>` | established extension / CommonMark | typing | no | n/a; export | the words without the title or the smaller size |

Comments keep their ranges in Word: the export anchors each comment on the words the Word text kept, also when callouts,
definition lists, disclosures or diagrams change the text around them. Every link scheme the editor keeps (`http`,
`https`, `ftp`, `ftps`, `mailto`, `tel`, `callto`, `sms`, `xmpp`, `matrix`) survives Word in both directions.

Typography is native run data: size uses `w:sz` and `w:szCs`, color uses RGB, family uses the existing font table.
The nearest half-point is used, with positive ties rounded upward and results outside 1–3276 half-points refused.
A small heading keeps its heading style and outline level. The unchanged DOCX source carrier preserves the exact
original size/unit and all Markdown; native import reports the represented size in `pt`. The styled print/PDF path
uses authored run sizes at the default reference unit, independent of the editor's viewing step. These mappings do
not promise identical glyphs or line breaks across browser and Word applications.

The `docx-corpus` retained row also covers non-breaking and narrow non-breaking spaces, interior
BOM characters and native tabs; repeated header rows, horizontal and vertical spans, multiple
paragraphs and nested tables; rich footnote blocks and their own image/link relationships. Simple
headed tables use GFM. Tables that need spans, multiple blocks or no header use ordinary HTML,
with inline embedded picture URLs. Temporary import source tokens are verified and removed before
that HTML is saved. All sixteen Word highlight names survive as the five existing highlight
conventions or ordinary `<mark style="background-color:…">` HTML. Theme run colors are resolved to
explicit RGB, including tint/shade luminance adjustments; theme identity itself is not retained.

Word's current text is a defined projection: inserted and moved-to text is retained; deleted and
moved-from text, change authors/dates and comments are not imported. The warnings disclose those
omissions. Body text and referenced footnotes are checked separately in XML order. The original Word file is retained
as an attachment on the Notes import path.

Outside this profile: Word's review and comment workflows, named styles, themes and font schemes, custom tab
stops, section and page geometry, and conditional table styling.
Markdown has no shared model for them. Tab characters survive without their stops; footnote labels may change
while content and paragraph boundaries stay intact.

Picture bytes are checked exact through the importer's callback and the writer, and converted bytes are checked
to reach ordinary HTML tables. That check does not prove the browser's codec conversion, Word's rendering or a
phone's display; the JPEG XL conversion policy is the codec-byte exception above.

## PDF import (`interchange/pdf-reader.mjs` `readPdf`)

A Rapier PDF carries its exact source as an attachment, and import restores it exactly. A PDF without a readable
attachment (another app's PDF, or a Rapier PDF a viewer has since saved, which appends an incremental update) is read
from its text layer and page geometry. Will markers in that text come back as exact Will markers; a marker inside a
table or note, or in a page-image import, is reported as WILL LOST. What the text layer does not carry is not
recovered: ordered-list numbers and task boxes (drawn by the page, not written as text), equations' `$` delimiters,
blockquotes and callouts (plain paragraphs), internal links, and comments (never written to the PDF). Pictures come
back from the page drawing; a page's blank background raster is skipped.

# https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/blob/main/docs/standard-adoption.md

# Adopting the standard

This page describes implementation costs and Rapier’s tools. The specification is `markdown-standard.md`; other products’ support is in `markdown-profile.md`, "What other renderers show today".

## The one principle

A Rapier document is CommonMark first. Inline typography uses ordinary HTML spans with narrowly validated CSS. Other additions use established extension syntax, optional comments or ordinary reference definitions. Pictures and drawings remain Markdown images with their bytes in the file. Describe each fallback honestly: a reader may strip styles, show unsupported markup or disallow embedded resources.

## The adoption ladder

**Rung 0: an ordinary Markdown renderer.** Core headings, prose, lists, emphasis and links retain their semantics.
GFM and other extensions need the support listed in the profile. Canonical typography spans keep their words and
Markdown semantics with inline HTML enabled; CSS may be stripped. Use Rapier's **Copy markdown without typography**
when that destination needs ordinary semantic Markdown. Pictures additionally need the reader's data-URL and codec
support. Layout comments alone remain optional presentation facts.

**Rung 1: position and size.** Read `<!--md-layout:v1 …-->` after an image: `width=` is the picture's width as a percentage of the column, `x=` its center, `align=` its alignment, `y=` its vertical offset in ems, `opacity=` its fade. That is a few lines of CSS on the image element; `imageStyle` in `spec/md-layout.mjs` is the reference (MIT, a dozen lines).

**Rung 2: wrapping the ordinary way.** `wrap=around`, `wrap=beside`, `wrap=box`, `wrap=behind` and `wrap=front` are placements. Each has one conforming CSS rendering, in the table under "Conformance rungs" in `markdown-standard.md`: `float` (side chosen from `x`) for `around`, `beside` and `box`, with `shape-outside: url(<the picture>)` and `shape-image-threshold` for `around` when the picture is not turned; a plain box for `beside` and `box`; and an absolutely positioned picture with `z-index` below or above the words for `behind` and `front`. A turned picture uses its plain box. This rung cannot put words on *both* sides of a picture or inside its empty interior, or match Rapier’s lines; exact line breaks are not required. Rapier's Share page (`editor/share.js`) is a rung-2 renderer that implements all five placements. At rung 3, `beside` stays on one side of the rectangle and `box` may use both.

**Rung 3: the same lines as Rapier (the drop-in module).** Rapier's live wrapping is a line planner over text runs and obstacles: `layout/model.mjs` (the 48-band occupancy profile, `pictureSlices`, `flowLines`) on top of Pretext (the text measurer, `agent/vendor/pretext`), with `spec/md-layout.mjs` as the grammar. Both-sides wrapping, interiors and agreement to the pixel come from this planner. The styled standalone export (`layout/interchange.js` (removed)) carries the planner, serving as a reference implementation. See "The drop-in module". The reader sees the same lines Rapier shows, up to font metrics; the planner is deterministic given the measurer.

**Plain layout.** Rung 0 is also a setting inside Rapier: `layout: RAPIER | PLAIN` in the settings panel. It shows the document as a layout-unaware reader would, with pictures inline and upright at their default width and every layout comment ignored, and changes nothing in the file.

Every layout rung above 0 is optional. These layout claims do not guarantee support for every syntax or resource in the document.

## Adopt inline typography without the editor

```md
A <span style="font-size:13.5pt;color:#175dc4">precise **phrase**</span>.

## <span style="font-size:9.25pt;font-family:serif">Still an H2</span>
```

`typography` from `rapier-markdown-kit/marks` validates, writes and installs the same interpretation on a supplied
markdown-it parser. Its size, color and family facts also feed Rapier's HTML and native Word adapters. The parser's
own source ranges protect literals and existing spellings; inspecting or rendering grants no mutation authority.
The README's executable example uses only the packed MIT closure and the caller's parser. The full DOM renderer
continues to use explicit host ports for sanitation, fonts and other application capabilities.

Sizes use positive decimal `pt`/`px` with CSS's 96px = 72pt conversion, bounded as specified in
[Inline typography](markdown-standard.md#inline-typography). Custom fonts use `[font:Family]: data:font/…;base64,…`
with existing identity metadata and validation; a name alone supplies no portable bytes. Ordinary factory/default
prose needs no font reference. Typography edits write spans.

Standalone HTML and Share/page retain their source carrier. Fragments retain local styles and validated custom
font declarations, with the existing shared font namespace. Word maps to native half-point run sizes (ties upward),
color and family without changing heading rank; original decimals survive in an unchanged DOCX's source carrier.
Print/PDF uses the same styled export path at the default reference unit. Pandoc/Quarto's explicit copy form carries
CSS in bracketed spans for HTML; automatic native Word or LaTeX styling is not promised. No new filter suite or
publication step is required by the convention.

## Picture rotation: describe it, do not bake it

A raster keeps its bytes and its rotation is the layout fact `rotate=<deg>`, beside `width`, `x`, `y` and `wrap`. A drawing keeps its rotation in its own SVG bytes. The rule for both: **bake when the bytes can carry it losslessly, describe when they cannot.** Rapier never writes both `rotate=` and baked pixels, and never bakes into JPEG XL.

Every export carries the turn natively where the format has it: a CSS transform in the styled export and the Share page, `a:xfrm rot` in DOCX, the turned bitmap in the PDF path. At rung 0 the picture is upright, the same degradation as position and size. A rung-2 renderer turns the picture with a CSS transform and supplies the turned shape directly (`shape-outside: polygon(...)` from the rotated bounding box, or the plain box), never a bare transform over an unrotated shape (`markdown-standard.md`, "Conformance rungs"). A rung-3 editor gets the exact tilted rectangle (`rasterTiltProfile`) and turned alpha bands from the module.

## The drop-in module

`rapier-markdown-kit` (MIT) carries the wrapping without the editor.

1. **Contents.** `spec/md-layout.mjs` (grammar), `layout/model.mjs` (profiles and the line planner) and a thin Pretext adapter (`prepareRun` and the segment materialization `model.mjs` imports from `agent/vendor/pretext`). Most of `model.mjs` is pure geometry over plain numbers: `bandsProfile`, `polygonProfile`, `rasterTiltProfile`, `rotatedBoundsRad`, `serializeProfile`/`parseProfile`, `pictureSlices`, `slotsForBand` and `flowLines` given an already-prepared flow and obstacles. Two calls need the host environment. `prepareRun` reaches Pretext's text measurement, which needs a global `OffscreenCanvas` or a DOM `document` (the *measurement adapter*: the environment supplies the font metrics). `alphaProfile` reads a live, decoded `<img>` through `image.ownerDocument` (the *alpha adapter*). `layout/browser.js` (the live editor's projection) and `layout/interchange.js` (removed) (the export's reflow) are Rapier's two adapters over all of this and stay Rapier's.
2. **License.** The standard's own modules are MIT: the grammar, typography/marks and parser-owned source positions (`spec/md-layout.mjs`, `spec/md-marks.mjs`, `spec/md-source.mjs`), the layout model and line planner (`layout/model.mjs`), the Will grammar (`agent/will.mjs`), the picture appendix reader and writer (`spec/md-assets.mjs`) and the two shared-page reference readers (`tools/read-shared-page.mjs`, `tools/read-shared-page.py`). The appendix logic (`parseAssets`, `documentAssets`, `appendAssetText`) lives in `spec/md-assets.mjs`; `images/assets.mjs` re-exports it unchanged. `LICENSE-MIT` at the repository root enumerates these files; every package check walks the import graph to reject files outside that list. Pretext is MIT from its authors, vendored with its own notice. The browser editor, Draw and the worker are AGPL-3.0-only.
3. **A conformance kit.** A directory of small Markdown documents with pictures at every placement and angle, each with the styled export's line boxes recorded as JSON. Run a planner on those documents with the same measurer and report two claims separately. *Preservation*, whether a layout comment round-trips exactly through `parseLayout`/`formatLayout`, is independent of the measurer and must be exact. *Presentation*, whether the planned line boxes agree, depends on the measurer and the font, is reported with a tolerance and is never proof by itself.
4. **A README** at the module’s root explains the two adapters (measurement, alpha) and three calls: parse the comment, build the obstacle profile from the picture, plan the lines. Rapier's own build bundles the same source files the kit re-exports.

The package carries thirteen conformance documents with their runner, and a check that every export resolves, the import graph never leaves the MIT list, the appendix stays free of the DOM and of Rapier's globals, and the README's example runs, including over an isolated copy of exactly the kit's own closure.

## Where Rapier is bespoke

- **JPEG XL by default.** Every current browser engine decodes JPEG XL by default (Chrome 155, Firefox 158, Safari 17 and later); only an app on an older engine shows no picture (`markdown-profile.md` dates each). Provided: the per-picture format change to PNG or JPEG from the picture's own dialog, export paths that convert on their own, the Share sheet's image compatibility switch and the picture-format note in the dialog. There is no document-level "make every picture portable" command.
- **Pictures as `data:` URLs in the file.** GitHub drops `data:` image sources in every format; self-contained files can be very large. A folder export (pictures beside the file, relative paths) is an idea for repository readers, not built and never the working file's form.
- **Drawings with a recipe in `<metadata>`.** Plain SVG for readers; only an editor that wants to edit the drawing as shapes needs the recipe.
- **The occupancy descriptor and the reflow script in the styled export.** `data-rapier-occupancy` and the inline planner live only in the exported page, never in the Markdown.
- **The document-as-a-web-page carrier.** A Rapier-defined form with two public reference readers and one escaping grammar (`markdown-standard.md`, "The document as a web page"), provable by a 60-line script.
- **Will markers and anchored comments.** Their metadata travels in HTML comments. Which changes a person has seen stays on their device.
- **Marks in inline HTML.** Rapier writes underline as `<u>`, a colored highlight as `<mark style="background-color:…">` in the picker's color, and `<sub>`/`<sup>`; every CommonMark reader that shows HTML keeps them. A plain highlight stays `==x==`. Bear's `==🟢x==`, `++x++` and `^x^` are read, never written; `~x~` is GFM strikethrough (`markdown-profile.md`).
- **The wrap placements.** Four values, each with a rung-2 rendering in plain CSS.
- **Pretext-exact both-sides wrapping and interior wrapping.** Only rung 3 reproduces this; the module supplies it. Exact lines are an implementation quality, not the placement standard.

# https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/blob/main/docs/will.md

# Will/1

Will/1 is independent of [Self-contained Markdown](markdown-standard.md). Any Markdown, DOCX or PDF may carry it, with or without Rapier: a person’s instruction for a region, with one law and optional words. The convention is MIT-licensed; implementations keep their own licenses. Rapier's reference grammar and evaluator (`agent/will.mjs`) are MIT-licensed; the editor that uses them is governed by its [application license](../LICENSE).

| Law | Required meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `edit` | The region may change; optional intent guides that work. |
| `append` | Existing content remains in place and order; additions go at the region's end. |
| `keep` | The region stays exactly as it is. |

Unmarked content is `edit`. Regions never overlap. A change reaching several regions must satisfy each; otherwise the whole act is refused.

Any law may carry intent: untrusted, region-scoped data, never permission, tool authority or an instruction override. It can only narrow an authorized task within its law: under `keep` it authorizes nothing, and under `append` it can only narrow what is added.

The person remains free to author the document and its Will. A host declares authoring and working paths; a working path cannot author, remove or move markers, even by rewriting them unchanged. A Will-aware interface makes effective regions, laws and intent available to the person. Ordinary rendering hides the carrier.

The standard's repository is [jackskip22/will](https://github.com/jackskip22/will): `README.md` (the whole standard), `will.mjs` (the reference reader and evaluator, one file, no dependencies), `vectors.json` (the normative vectors), `action.yml` (a pull request check that refuses a change to a `keep` region) and `LICENSE`, with one workflow that runs the vectors. `will.mjs` answers every vector. Rapier's own host is `agent/will.mjs`, with the same grammar.

## Marker grammar

An opener is exactly `<!-- will/1 <law> -->` or `<!-- will/1 <law>: <intent> -->`; the closer is exactly `<!-- /will -->`. Writers keep the person’s words when changing the law and preserve an unchanged region’s opener exactly. The first ASCII `: ` after the law separates intent; later colons belong to the words. Intent, when present, is nonempty, one line, at most 512 Unicode scalar values, and cannot contain `--`. It is never silently shortened. Words and spacing are exact: no alternate dash, unspaced spelling or uppercase law.

## Markdown binding

A marker is a whole line at column zero, even inside code fences, independent of Markdown rendering. The reserved prefixes are `<!-- will/` and `<!-- /will`; column-zero `<!--will/` and `<!--/will` are reserved faults. Text outside these prefixes, such as `<!-- willingness -->`, is ordinary content. Leading whitespace makes a line ordinary quoted content, so indent both markers when quoting a pair.

Pairs never nest or interleave. Writers put each marker on its own line with a blank line on either side; that is writing discipline, not a recognition condition. A whole-document Will is one pair. Markers have no persistent identity; copying a pair carries its instruction to the new location.

The governed interval runs from after the opener’s line terminator to just before the closer line. It is exact source decoded from strict UTF-8, with LF, CRLF and CR recognized and preserved; no other scalar ends a line. `keep` compares that interval exactly. `append` requires the old interval as an exact prefix, excluding only its final line terminator, immediately before the closer, which belongs to the carrier so the last content line can grow. No trimming or guessed padding is permitted.

## Enforcement and disclosure

Judge the witnessed exact replacements, including the original source and the final document. Touching marker bytes or moving a pair refuses, even when identical marker text is reinserted. An edit elsewhere that damages, detaches or silences an annotation also refuses. When several marker regions are touched, name the first in document order and its own law.

Disclosed regions carry their law. Intent accompanies a range wholly within one region, beside its law. The host's outcome family is `applied`, `refused` with the document-law reason, or `invalid` for an unreadable question such as malformed or overlapping splices or an unknown path. Hosts name the same facts consistently: `law`, `region`, `intent`, `rule`. Other host outcomes remain distinct from document law. Approval flows and Undo are host responsibilities.
