Mount snapshots a record; a callback is called again after each connection to request the host's current record.
The `save` callback receives `{content, filename, docKind, codeLang, requestId, baseRevision}` and returns
`{revision}` directly or through a promise, only after durable storage confirms the write. A repeated request ID
shares the first write and repeats its first answer, even while that write is pending. A repeated ID with different source, metadata or base revision is refused as
`save_request_conflict`. Source must fit the session's UTF-8 document byte limit before it reaches your callback.
Oversized source is `document_too_large`; ill-formed Unicode and malformed metadata are `save_payload_invalid`.
The helper holds answers for its lifetime; your store must also deduplicate IDs across host
reloads. Choose the draft identity described below when you intend to recover a session.

Switch documents with `editor.load(content, {revision, filename})` or `editor.load({content, revision, filename})`. `revision` is optional in `load()`: left out, the helper uses one above the last revision it saw, or 1. `mount`'s `load` needs it. A load always shows and saves the document you gave it. It is refused by code while the person has unsaved edits (`unsaved_changes`; call `save()` first), and for the same filename with a revision older than the frame's (`revision_stale`) or with the same revision and other content (`revision_conflict`). Another filename is another document with its own revisions.

Reading the text: the editor sends source only to your `save` callback. `save()` with no edits since the last load or save resolves the current revision and does not call your callback. There is no read that skips `save`; keep the last saved text in memory if you need it.

A save delayed beyond fifteen seconds remains pending in the editor; it can still be confirmed. `editor.save()`
waits for the editor to accept the durable revision with its latest edits saved. An unacknowledged write never
becomes a successful save because time passed. On conflict, throw `Rapier.conflict(currentRevision)`; the person's
source stays in the editor.

## Session settings and picture storage

```js
const editor = Rapier.mount(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  src: '/vendor/rapier/rapier.html',
  settings: {
    features: ['find', 'share'],
    language: 'en',
    limits: {documentBytes: 4 * 1024 * 1024, pictureBytes: 2 * 1024 * 1024},
    palette: {accent: 'Blue'},
  },
  load: {content: documentText, filename: 'notes.md', revision: storedRevision},
  save: async request => documents.storeOnce(request), // return an advancing durable {revision}
  assets: async ({requestId, bytesSha256, mediaType, bytes, signal}) => {
    // Your authenticated storage API must bind this request to the current user's document,
    // verify the content, deduplicate durably, and serve these exact bytes at the returned URL.
    const response = await fetch('/api/document-pictures', {
      method: 'POST', signal,
      headers: {'Content-Type': mediaType, 'Idempotency-Key': requestId, 'X-Content-SHA256': bytesSha256},
      body: bytes,
    });
    if (!response.ok) throw Object.assign(new Error('Picture storage refused'), {code: 'storage_refused'});
    const {url} = await response.json();
    return {url}; // absolute HTTPS; no credentials; at most 4,096 code units
  },
});
await editor.ready;
```

`settings` is optional, snapshotted before navigation and frozen for that frame's session. `connected` events
carry the accepted settings (register `editor.on('connected', fn)` immediately after mounting). They are not
written over personal preferences. Features are a subset of `draw`, `paint`, `notes`, `readAloud`, `share` and
`find`; absent means everything that build has, empty means none. The reader carries no Draw,
Paint or Notes. This release carries only English; another valid BCP 47 tag falls back to `en`. Unknown features and
malformed fields are named refusals, not ignored options. Limits are positive integer byte counts, clamped to
64 MiB of UTF-8 document text and 16 MiB of encoded picture bytes. Accent preset names are `Teal`, `Blue`,
`Amber`, `Green`, `Red`, `Purple`, `Pink` and `Gray`; the person's later choice takes precedence.

`assets` is independently optional: it grants pictures, not document readback, opening, agents or changes.
The helper verifies each request's type, byte bound and SHA-256 before calling storage. Repeated request IDs
share the callback and first result; a changed repeat is refused. The helper keeps 48 outcomes and at most one
pending callback. Your store still needs durable idempotence across that window and reloads. An aborted `signal`
means the connection retired; honor it for cancellable work. A host callback can still have stored bytes when
it fails or is retired, so orphan cleanup and access control belong to your application.

The frame waits up to 15 seconds for a picture acknowledgment, then inserts its embedded bytes instead; this
is not Save's late-acknowledgment rule. Nack, no grant and unavailable storage also keep single-file insertion.
On ack, the Markdown contains a normal URL image. The frame previews and reopens it from retained local bytes,
never by fetching the host address back. Local previews are scoped to the current document and bounded by
1,024 URLs and 25 MiB. Ordinary picture and document limits still apply to the fallback. Storage durability and
correct serving at the URL remain the host's promise. Changing a document while storage is pending cannot
apply the old insertion to the replacement document. Asset failures do not reject an unrelated Save.

## The handle and its grants

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `build` | `'full'` (default; `rapier.html`, also named `'document'`) or `'reader'` |
| `src` | Your copy of the page; omitted, the hosted current build |
| `sessionId`, `documentId` | The fixed draft identity for this handle; see Draft identity below |
| `load` | Grants `open` |
| `save` | Grants `read`, plus `changes` to observe save completion |
| `onState(state)` | Grants `changes` |
| `compare: true` | Grants `compare` |
| `onClose({dirty})` | Grants `close`; return `save`, `discard` or `cancel` |
| `agent: true` | Grants `agent`; requires both `load` and `save` |
| `agentName` | The name the editor shows for your app's agent, at most 96 characters |
| `assets(request)` | Grants `assets` only; the callback stores picture bytes and returns `{url}` |
| `settings`, `theme`, `style` | Session settings, `'light'`, `'dark'` or `'system'`, and the reader's look |
| `plugins` | The directory that holds the page's plug-in files, on the page's own origin (a relative address is read from your page); the page then fetches from nowhere else. Either build |
| `approvePlugins` | `true`: install math and diagram plug-ins without asking the person. Naming `plugins` does the same. Default `false` |
| `title`, `onError(error)` | The iframe's accessible title, and an error listener |
| `timeout` | Milliseconds after the frame loads that it has to connect before `ready` rejects with `connect_timeout`; default 15000 |

The handle has `iframe`, `ready` (a promise) and `connected`. `load(content, {revision, filename?, readOnly?,
title?, baseUrl?})`, `save()`, `compare(content, {filename?})` and `close()` use their grants. `theme(value)` changes
the host theme; `style({css, fonts})` restyles the reader. `ready` resolves after connection and the initial load,
when supplied. The `connected` event identifies a live connection; it does not mean that the document has loaded.
The original `ready` promise is not replaced on reconnect.

A created iframe has 100% width and height and no border; your CSS can override those attributes. Give its
container a height. Mount adds the frame after what the container already holds: clear a server-rendered
placeholder first (`container.replaceChildren()`).

### Lifecycle

| Transition | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Mount | Fix the IDs, grants and settings before navigation. Snapshot an initial load record, or call its loader after connection. |
| Accepted load | Keep the complete record: content, revision, filename, readOnly, title and baseUrl. A refused load leaves the last accepted record intact. |
| Confirmed Save | Keep the identity, update the saved content and revision, and wait for the frame to hold no newer edits before `save()` resolves. |
| Iframe navigation or reload | Reject old pending operations. Replay the last accepted record, updated by confirmed saves, when `load` was an object; call a function loader again for the current record. |
| Port error | Retire the connection and reject pending calls with `disconnected`. Recovery waits for a later iframe load. |
| Move within one task | Keep the connection if the iframe is attached when removal is observed. |
| Observed removal | Set `connected` to false, reject pending calls with `frame_removed` and release the active ID pair. The handle keeps its recovery state and iframe load listener. |
| Reinsert the same iframe | Reconnect that handle if it was not explicitly disconnected and the ID pair is free. If another writer owns the pair, refuse with `document_open_elsewhere`. Retired operations do not resume. |
| `disconnect()` | End the handle permanently, even while detached; reject unfinished operations and release ports, listeners, observers and timers. Remove an iframe mount created; leave an iframe you supplied. A new mount gets a new handle. |

Removal, reconnect and `disconnect()` do not save or discard the document. There is no autosave on unmount. A
late callback from an old connection cannot acknowledge work on its replacement; storage it already performed
remains your application's responsibility. A matching draft can be recovered as described below.

An editor iframe you supplied keeps its loaded document and its claim after disconnection. Another frame with
the same ID pair remains refused while that document is open. Remove or navigate the supplied iframe before
another frame opens the pair. Ending the transport does not discard the retained unsaved words.

Tab walks every control and link in the frame, except inside the editor text, where Tab indents. Escape, with nothing open in the frame and no text field focused, moves
focus to the next control on your page after the frame; Shift+Escape moves it to the control before. From the editor text the way out is Escape, then Tab (Shift+Tab goes back).
`on('connected' | 'state' | 'close-request' | 'closed' | 'error', fn)` returns an
unsubscribe function. State is `{loaded, dirty, saving, closing, readOnly, filename, docKind}`. Mount a fresh frame to
change grants or settings. A denied or dirty replacement load rejects.

Every refusal is an `Error` with a `code`. A connect the frame refuses rejects `ready`: `contract_unsupported`,
`capabilities_invalid`, a `settings_*` code, or `invalid_payload` with a `reason`. A frame that cannot start rejects
`ready` and calls `onError`: `boot_failed` when the page shows its startup error, `connect_timeout` when it does not connect
within `timeout` of loading, or `load_timeout` when the page or first document exceeds its load bound. `load()`
rejects with `load_timeout` when the frame does not answer within that bound, `load_busy` while an earlier load is
still being shown, `invalid_payload` for malformed input, `invalid_filename` or `invalid_base_url` for those
fields, `load_failed` when the frame cannot finish loading, and `document_unshowable` when the reader cannot
show the document; the reader keeps the document it showed. A document over 1 MB resolves `load()` when its first screen shows; the reader draws the rest after it. It rejects with `revision_stale` for a
revision older than the frame's and `revision_conflict` for the same revision with other content. It rejects with `document_open_elsewhere` when another editor already has the same `sessionId` and `documentId` open (on mount, `ready` rejects with it); the first editor keeps its typing. `mount` throws a
`TypeError` with a code for an unknown option (`option_unknown`), a build whose `src` names the other page (`build_mismatch`)
and a reader feature the reader does not have (`settings_feature_unavailable`). `Rapier.version` is this package's version;
`handle.version` and `handle.contract` are the frame's, once connected. `load()` resolves `{revision, recoveredDraft,
readOnly}`; `compare()` resolves `{filename}`. `save()` resolves with
`{revision}` once the frame holds no newer edits (with no edits since the last load or save, the current revision, and
your callback is not called), and rejects with `conflict`, `failed` (your callback threw),
`document_too_large`, `save_payload_invalid`, `not_loaded` (no load yet), `read_only` or `save_unavailable` (the
frame could not capture; the person is told why). `close()` resolves with the frame's `close-ready` payload:
`{saved: true}` or `{discarded: true}` after your answer, `{forced: true}` when the person closes without your
answer, or `{cancelled: true}` when you answer `cancel`.

### Draft identity

| Mount options | Identity |
| --- | --- |
| Both `sessionId` and `documentId` | The exact pair you supply. |
| `documentId` and `save`, with no `sessionId` | Your document ID and a stable session derived from the host's origin and path. |
| Neither ID, with `save` and a `load` object | An automatic pair derived from the host page, filename, loaded text and an available matching-document slot. |
| Other omitted IDs | Generated IDs; provide your own stable pair for recovery across new mounts. |

The chosen IDs stay fixed for the handle. Changing filename changes the document's revision rules, not those
IDs. A second live mount of the same pair on a page is refused before its frame loads: `ready` rejects with
`document_open_elsewhere`, and the first keeps its document. Retire the first frame's document before another
frame acquires that pair; disconnect removes a helper-created frame, while a supplied frame needs removal or
navigation. Recovery after a route change, unmount or reload needs the same IDs, saved revision
and content in the same tab. Form replacements have the further limit described below.

`save()` and `requestSubmit()` ask the frame to capture its current text. With nothing unsaved, the frame answers
at once and the save callback is not called.

The frame keeps the person's unsaved work only for the document you loaded: a draft in that tab's session storage,
which a load of the same revision and content reopens and your `discard` answer retires. A load of another document drops a draft with no unsaved edits. It never reads, offers or writes the
person's own Rapier documents or recovery on its origin, and it keeps nothing before your first load.

Saving names the browser-authenticated host and port. The helper's acknowledgment is your statement that storage
succeeded; Rapier cannot make an arbitrary host keep that promise. To show saved documents without a frame, use
`rapier-markdown-kit`, the same renderer as a library.

## A form field

```html
<form method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
  <label for="body">Document</label>
  <rapier-editor id="body" name="body" required src="/vendor/rapier/rapier.html">
    <textarea name="body"># Notes

Write here.</textarea>
  </rapier-editor>
  <button name="action" value="publish">Publish</button>
</form>
<script type="module">
  import {defineRapierEditor} from 'rapier-embed';
  defineRapierEditor();
</script>
```

The textarea works without script. After upgrade, `element.value` is the exact captured Markdown;
`await element.save()` captures the current source and returns that string. `change` fires when captured text
updates the field. Submit captures the edited source first, then continues native form validation and
submission with its submitter. Use `requestSubmit()` for scripted submissions; `form.submit()` bypasses submit events and cannot
capture pending edits.

The successful field is a `text/markdown` file part named `body`: read its uploaded bytes on the server, or
`await new FormData(form).get('body').text()` in JavaScript. A file part preserves LF, CRLF and image data
exactly; native text parts normalize line endings. The restoration state and `value` remain strings. Pictures
already live in the Markdown, so use `multipart/form-data`.

Reset restores the initial text. Assigning `value` selects that exact string; when the browser supplies a string
for form state restoration, the field restores it exactly. Each replacement retires pending field work and
selects fresh draft IDs held in the element's memory. A late capture cannot overwrite the replacement or resume
an old form submission.

On its first mount, a field with a DOM `id` derives its identity from the host page, initial filename and text,
and that ID. A field without an ID uses the automatic matching-document slot rule. Both kinds keep their chosen
IDs across removal and reinsertion of the same element. The fresh IDs selected by Reset, value assignment or
state restoration are also kept across that same-element remount, so typing after the replacement can recover.

A full host-page reload creates a new element and loses the replacement's in-memory IDs. The host or browser
must restore its replacement value. Recreating the original automatic identity can reopen a pre-Reset draft;
it cannot find later typing kept under the replacement's generated IDs. The helper does not erase that earlier
session-storage draft or persist the replacement identity in another store.

`required`, `disabled`, labels, focus and native validity methods work as a field's do. Disabling first keeps
any pending edits, then makes the editor read-only and excludes the field from submission. A phone opens its text preview in a
full-screen editor; a wide screen edits inline. Resizing keeps the same editor session. Listen for `error` to
report a refused capture without submitting stale text. Form saves hold the source in the field until
submission; they are not durable server saves.

## Work with your app's agent

With `agent: true`, the frame registers Rapier's tools through WebMCP for your page's origin; the
browser needs WebMCP and the `tools` permission, which mount grants the frame. Where WebMCP is still an origin
trial, the published pages carry the trial token for `rapier.website` only: serve your own copy with your origin's
WebMCP trial token (an `Origin-Trial` response header). After `disconnect`, the tools refuse with
`host_not_connected`; the document stays in the frame for the person to copy or download. There is no arbitrary `invoke`
postMessage. The tools are `open`, `read`, `edit`, `undo`, `show` and `export`, as on the hosted door
(see the [agent guide](https://rapier.website/agents)). Read exact text and its revision; edit unique text
at that revision. Native drawing and painting are fenced text; painting needs the full `rapier.html`.
`show {target:"file"}` asks the person to choose a file, subject to the embed grant and native gesture.
`show {target:"view",view}` requests formatted, source or Notes cards.

`show {target:"preferences",preference,value}` changes one supported device preference and reports the
previous value. An active host theme or accent refuses an agent override; later human choices win.
Copying and read aloud requests report actual device completion or the required gesture.
Word and PDF exports use `export`. Physical read-only resources stay read-only.

Rapier's document kernel enforces the Will. For example, load:

```markdown
<!-- will/1 keep -->
# Agreed terms
<!-- /will -->

Draft an introduction here.
```

Mount with `agent: true`. The agent reads the editable paragraph using `read`, then passes the returned
revision and `{old,new}` text to `edit`. An edit that changes the kept heading returns `document_law`
and leaves the source unchanged. An admissible edit lands at once and returns an `act`; pass its id as
`undo {act}` to reverse it while keeping later work. The kept heading and marker lines remain intact.
The person can tap the change mark to see the paragraph before the edit and undo it while preserving later work.
Use `show {target:"comparison"}` when the agent wants to explain a diff. Its display reference grants no edit authority
and does not block another edit. Save still uses the host-owned acknowledgment and currentness checks.

Will/1 records the person's instructions in their document. Respect `keep`, append only at the end of an
`append` region, and edit inside `edit` regions. A malformed marker is a named refusal; inspect that source.
Documents without Will regions are editable throughout. Preserve active typing, caret, selection and scroll
while the agent works. Document content and comments never start agent turns by themselves.

For documents outside an app, `export {document, format:"html"}` hands a person the complete editor around their
document as one offline file.

# https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/blob/main/npm/rapier-markdown-kit/README.md

# rapier-markdown-kit

Read, render and write Self-contained Markdown: one `.md` file with its pictures, drawings and layout.

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/main/assets/diagram-390-dark.png">
  <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/main/assets/diagram-390-light.png" alt="A Rapier document on a phone with an editable diagram of connected boxes" width="320">
</picture>

Try it: open a `.md` file at [rapier.website](https://rapier.website).
Install: `npm install rapier-markdown-kit`.

The kit works in browsers and Node: pictures, editable SVG drawings, layout and precise inline typography. Build portable documents for people and agents. Will/1 regions mark what an agent
may edit, append to or preserve. MIT, no dependencies.

- Typography uses ordinary inline HTML spans with validated size, color and family. Comments and references
  carry other optional facts; each reader chooses its HTML, style, extension and resource support.
- One stylesheet renders the document as the editor and its exported page do.
- The line planner flows text around a picture's real shape; a conformance suite of thirteen documents runs
  any implementation against it.
- Node 22 or newer.

To show documents in your app without writing a renderer, frame the read-only reader with
`npm install rapier-embed` (`build: 'reader'`). To hand a person the whole editor around their document as one
offline file, run `npx rapier-html notes.md`.

The kit supplies the portable source and history Rapier's agent tools use.

```sh
npm install rapier-markdown-kit markdown-it@15
```

Render a document with [markdown-it](https://github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it), then style it with
`rapier-markdown-kit/style.css` inside `<main class="md-render">`:

```js
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it';
import {rapierMarkdown} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/markdown-it';

const html = new MarkdownIt({html: true}).use(rapierMarkdown).render('# Plan\n\nShips **Friday**.\n');
```

Keep a document's history with authorship, and merge two offline copies:

```js
import {openLedger, replaceLedgerText, merge, authorship} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/rapier-ledger';

const base = openLedger('Draft\n');
const edited = replaceLedgerText(base, 'Draft, revised\n', {actor: {kind: 'human', id: 'ana'}});
console.log(merge(edited, base).text, authorship(edited).runs);
```

TypeScript declarations ship for the root and every JavaScript subpath. NodeNext and bundler resolution use the same public exports. DOM host APIs use TypeScript’s `DOM` library; pure history and Will consumers can import their own subpaths. The Markdown rendering examples install `markdown-it` explicitly; the kit itself has no npm dependencies.

```js
import {parseLayout} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/layout';   // the md-layout comment a picture carries
import {typography, formatPageBreak} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/marks';   // inline typography and page breaks
import {flowLines} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/model';      // the line planner: text around pictures
import {parseWill} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/will';       // Will/1 markers: keep, append, edit
import {parseAssets} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/assets';   // the picture appendix
```

## Choose a Rapier workflow

Rapier is a phone-first Markdown editor for notes, diagrams, drawing and watercolor painting. It runs offline
as one HTML file on Android, Web, Windows and Linux.

1. **Work together live.** Connect to `https://mcp.rapier.website/door/mcp`, then call `open` to share one document with the person.
2. **Deliver an offline editor.** Run `npx rapier-html notes.md` to put the document and editor in one HTML file ([rapier-html](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/tree/main/npm/rapier-html)).
3. **Embed in your app.** Install [rapier-embed](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/tree/main/npm/rapier-embed); mount the editor or reader, with your app's agent over WebMCP in the editor.
4. **Keep portable Markdown.** Use [rapier-markdown-kit](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/tree/main/npm/rapier-markdown-kit) for pictures, editable SVG drawings and layout in one `.md` file. Respect [Will/1](https://github.com/jackskip22/will) `keep`, `append` and `edit` regions.
5. **Encode JPEG XL.** Install [rapier-jxl](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-jxl) to encode pixels, photographs and existing JPEGs in JavaScript.
6. **Host the door.** Run [rapier-server](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/tree/main/server) over your own folder or S3-compatible bucket.

## The shared renderer

To render Markdown in your own app, use `rapier-markdown-kit/markdown-it` (above). The render factories below are the
editor's own seam: each needs a `host` that supplies its DOM, Markdown, picture, style and font ports.

`rapier-markdown-kit/render` exports `createRenderer`, `createMarkdownRenderer`,
`createRenderStyles`, `createRenderSanitizer` and `createPrintRenderer`, plus the explicit font helpers
`exportFontCss`, `requireDocumentFonts`, `fontRequests`, `waitForFonts` and `waitForFontRequests`. These are the
functions used by the editor and exported pages. Each factory takes explicit host dependencies
in its first argument. Refined print paragraphs use the host's retained `RapierArtifactLayoutDependencies`
(the same factory graph used by standalone HTML). They initialize in the print document so its own font set
owns every measurement. Missing factories or a blocked initialization refuse the export. `style.css` is the
MIT `spec/markdown-style.css`, including the numbered-list, checkbox, callout, table,
footnote and picture-layout treatment.

```js
import {createRenderer} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/render';

// host binds the DOM, Markdown, image, style and font capabilities described below.
// Preparation returns a detached semantic root; source comes from this captured request.
const writer = createRenderer(host);
const {html, filename} = await writer.render(source, {filename: 'report.md'});
```

`createMarkdownRenderer(host).render(source, metadata)` returns the semantic HTML.
`createMarkdownRenderer(host).renderWithMathML(source, metadata)` returns
`{html, equations}` using the ready host math provider's `renderWithMathML` operation.
The provider must also support the existing `renderToString` operation.
Each equation is parsed once for its SVG and MathML. The HTML stays identical to
ordinary SVG rendering; `equations` follows render order and carries `source`
(the admitted token spelling, including its delimiters), `tex`, `displayMode`, `semantics`, and SVG
`errors`. Pass `{docKind: 'markdown'}` as metadata for Markdown documents.
The existing Markdown grammar may normalize display-block indentation; the original
document remains the source of untouched document bytes.
Inspect both `errors` and `semantics.status`: a rendered SVG can have refused or
partial semantic output. The method throws if the combined provider is unavailable
or fails, rather than returning an empty semantic success. It does not return an AST.

This explicit method makes structured output available to consuming applications;
Rapier's live editor and ordinary HTML/DOCX/print exports still use the current
engine's Latin Modern SVG path. They do not insert hidden MathML, synthesize speech,
or claim screen-reader qualification. A consumer that inserts MathML must preserve
its namespace and semantics/annotation elements, name enclosing links meaningfully,
and qualify its own accessibility presentation. The current ordinary document
sanitizer is not a MathML composition API.

The page writer's `render` returns `{html, filename}` asynchronously and preserves the
original source, including BOM and line endings, in the SHA-256-verified source carrier.
Every existing lower-level method is also returned for hosts that compose the stages.
Create a new bound instance when its parser or host state changes; do not share mutable
DOM objects between document realms.

This **DOM-hosted library** requires a DOM and sanitizer, the Rapier grammar,
portable image preparation, style access and the named codec/layout ports it uses.
Those dependencies keep their own licenses: the MIT grant here does not relicense a
separately supplied host or vendor. The [editor host binding](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/blob/main/src/editor/render-host.js)
lists the renderer's dependencies. [rapier-server](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/blob/main/server/README.md)
provides a complete local host with a pinned Chromium process. Its Word exporter and filesystem service are AGPL,
not part of this MIT package.

Serialization tests preserve source bytes through HTML export and recovery. Server integration
tests also check the exported HTTP response through a browser DOM.

### A complete prose host

For a small browser integration, save the following as `prose-host.mjs` and bundle it with your application. Install its explicit host dependencies with `npm install markdown-it@15.0.3 dompurify@3.4.16`. This host handles prose, headings, lists, tables and fenced code. It refuses front matter, media and diagram providers that it does not supply; the factories’ larger host contracts remain available in their declarations.

<details>
<summary>Browser host source</summary>

```js
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// A small browser host. Rendering and carrier algorithms come from the installed kit.
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it';
import createDOMPurify from 'dompurify';
import {rapierMarkdown} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/markdown-it';
import {createMarkdownRenderer, createRenderer, createRenderSanitizer, createRenderStyles, createPrintRenderer} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/render';
import {parseWill} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/will';

export function createProseHost({contentCss, validateFont, materializeDocumentFonts, parseAsync} = {}) {
  const md = new MarkdownIt({html: true}).use(rapierMarkdown);
  const purify = createDOMPurify(window);
  const state = {context: 'render'};
  const remote = {allowed: false};
  const reject = feature => { throw Object.assign(new Error('This example host does not provide ' + feature), {code: 'host_capability_unavailable'}); };
  // This example has no front-matter settings or media/provider resolver. Refuse
  // those capabilities before creating an artifact, instead of silently dropping them.
  const admitSource = source => {
    if (/^(?:\uFEFF)?---(?:\r\n|\r|\n)/.test(source)) reject('front-matter settings');
    if (/!\[|<(?:img|video|audio|iframe|svg)\b/i.test(source)) reject('media resources');
    if (/^\s*```(?:mermaid|math)\b/m.test(source)) reject('diagram/math providers');
    return source;
  };
  const cssHasResource = value => /(?:url|image-set|image|paint)\s*\(|@import/i.test(value);
  const sanitizer = createRenderSanitizer({
    CSSStyleSheet, DOMPurify: purify, URL, document, globalThis, location,
    RAPIER_RASTER_DATA_URL_RE: /^data:image\/(png|jpeg|gif|webp|jxl|svg\+xml);base64,([a-z0-9+/=]+)$/i,
    _rapierSanitizeRuntime: state, _rapierRemoteContent: remote,
    _rapierCssDeclaration: () => document.createElement('span').style,
    _rapierDropRemoteDeclarations: style => {
      let removed = false;
      for (const property of [...style]) if (cssHasResource(style.getPropertyValue(property))) {
        style.removeProperty(property); removed = true;
      }
      return removed;
    },
    _rapierRuleDescriptorIsRemote: rule => cssHasResource(rule.cssText),
  });
  sanitizer._rapierInstallDocumentSanitizeHooks();
  const styles = createRenderStyles({
    _rapierArtifactAccent: () => '#2673c9',
    _rapierStyleText: id => {
      if (id === 'rapier-content-style') return contentCss;
      // The host uses system fonts and plain escaped code, with no extra sheets.
      if (id === 'rapier-font-style' || id === 'rapier-highlight-style') return '';
      return reject('stylesheet ' + id);
    },
  });
  let writer;
  const headingsIn = (root, selector) => {
    const result = [...root.querySelectorAll(selector)];
    for (const template of root.querySelectorAll('template')) result.push(...headingsIn(template.content, selector));
    return result;
  };
  const markdown = createMarkdownRenderer({
    md, parseAsync, Node, document, window, globalThis,
    ...sanitizer,
    RAPIER_RENDERED_HEADING_SELECTOR: 'h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6',
    _rapierRemoteContent: remote, _rapierProviders: {},
    _rapierRenderedAnchorOriginalIds: new WeakMap(),
    _rapierDormantHeadings: headingsIn,
    // Anchor spelling is the host's policy. The renderer owns assignment and collisions.
    _rapierHeadingSlugBase: text => 'section-' + text.normalize('NFC').toLowerCase().replace(/[^\p{Letter}\p{Number}]+/gu, '-').replace(/^-|-$/g, ''),
    _rapierNextHeadingSlug: (base, used) => {
      let key = base, n = 1;
      while (Object.hasOwn(used, key)) key = base + '-' + ++n;
      used[key] = 0;
      return key;
    },
    _rapierSplitOpeningFrontmatter: source => ({body: admitSource(source)}),
    _rapierPrefixPortableAnchors: (...args) => writer._rapierPrefixPortableAnchors(...args),
  });
  writer = createRenderer({
    md, Node, document, crypto, globalThis, ...sanitizer, ...styles,
    // BOM is file metadata. Preserve every other source code unit, including EOLs.
    RapierTextCodec: {maxDocumentBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024, normalizeDocument: source => admitSource(source.charCodeAt(0) === 0xfeff ? source.slice(1) : source)},
    // This independent page has no Rapier application return address or edit ledger.
    RapierPageReturnAddress: {PAGE_SEED: ''},
    _rapierArtifactPreference: (name, allowed) => ({theme: 'light', highlights: 'standard', invertImageAlpha: 'false'})[name] || allowed[0],
    _rapierArtifactHighlight: source => sanitizer.escapeRapierHtmlText(source),
    _rapierLanguageClass: code => [...code.classList].find(name => name.startsWith('language-'))?.slice(9) || '',
    _rapierDocumentNameIsAdmissible: name => typeof name === 'string' && !!name && !/[\\/\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/.test(name),
    _rapierPrepareInterchangeContext: async (_options, captured) => ({...captured,
      semanticRoot: await markdown._rapierRenderSemanticRootAsync(captured.canonical, captured.metadata)}),
    _rapierProjectPortableRoot: (...args) => markdown._rapierProjectPortableRoot(...args),
    _rapierPortableHtml: (...args) => markdown._rapierPortableHtml(...args),
    validateFont, materializeDocumentFonts,
  });
  const print = createPrintRenderer({Node, crypto, document, globalThis, _rapierWillParse: parseWill});
  return {md, markdown, writer, print, sanitizer, styles, purify};
}
```

</details>

Use your bundler or static server to load the installed `style.css` text as `contentCss`, then call `createProseHost({contentCss})`. Its `markdown.render(source, {docKind: 'markdown'})` produces a fragment; `await writer.render(source, {filename: 'report.md'})` produces a complete offline page carrying the exact source. Keep one bound host per document realm: the Markdown factory registers an original-file listener and currently has no disposal method. The font and print operations have their own cleanup contracts.

The example is MIT. The host dependencies keep their licenses: markdown-it is MIT, and DOMPurify is Apache-2.0 OR MPL-2.0. Neither is an implicit dependency of the kit.

### Fonts in exported HTML

Settings HTML and Share pages use the same offline font policy. The writer reads custom font
definitions from the captured Markdown and carries their exact bytes and face metadata. A used
custom family must have valid embedded data; otherwise export stops without changing the document.
Font preparation and binary validation are explicit host capabilities:

| Host port | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `materializeDocumentFonts(source, {parser})` | Optional at `render()` entry; returns the prepared Markdown string or a promise for it. Without this port, the caller supplies already portable, captured Markdown. Materialization must preserve explicit font authority and return source for this request. |
| `validateFont(bytes, {family, format})` | Validates a `Uint8Array` and returns exactly `true`, synchronously or asynchronously, only on admission. Required used custom fonts refuse with `export_font_unavailable` if the port is absent and `export_font_invalid` if it returns another value. Host errors and cancellation propagate. |

Browser hosts additionally check the exact captured container with an uninstalled `FontFace`.
Without `FontFace`, only the host validator's admission is established; it does not establish
browser container support. The HTML font helpers do not bundle the application's font importer,
container codecs or subsetter. Rapier binds its existing materializer and shared importer at `editor/render-host.js` through
`editor/export-fonts.mjs`; those implementations retain their application license.
An embedded family named Geist or Geist Mono remains custom data and takes precedence over the
factory family. Custom fonts have no optional factory size limit.

Factory typography may add a genuine subset of Geist Sans for the page's actual text, using the
host's subsetter. `exportFontCss` accepts `subset` and `validateFont` ports; with `portableFactory:true`,
missing or unsuccessful validation omits this optional CSS. The complete set of used factory faces must fit both 8 KiB of font payload and
12 KiB of emitted font CSS, including base64. If subsetting is unavailable, unsafe, unchanged or too
large, the page uses the existing local/system fallback. HTML never carries factory Geist Mono;
code and native diagram labels retain their existing monospace fallbacks. No font is downloaded
when the saved file is opened, and optional factory fonts never enter the carried Markdown.

Publishing HTML remains a fragment: it carries only its custom font declarations and local
body, heading, code and inline choices, without a page wrapper or a factory bundle. The host must
permit inline styles and data fonts. Two fragments with different custom faces under the same
family name share the host's font namespace. Print retains its existing factory font policy.

## What it gives you

| Import | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `rapier-markdown-kit/markdown-it` | `md.use(rapierMarkdown)`: the reference style's markup in markdown-it, in one line, with rung 1 of `md-layout:v1` (align, indents, list markers, picture width, lines and opacity, paragraph typography). |
| `rapier-markdown-kit/parsed` | A frozen, serializable view of completed Markdown tokens, bound to source, revision and grammar. |
| `rapier-markdown-kit/layout` | The `md-layout:v1` comment a picture carries: parse it, validate it, write it back. |
| `rapier-markdown-kit/marks` | Unified typography values, span writer and parser installer; preserved color/font comments, ink and page breaks. |
| `rapier-markdown-kit/model` | Occupancy profiles and the line planner: the wrapping itself. |
| `rapier-markdown-kit/typography` | Source-preserving paragraph refinement through `createTypography()`. |
| `rapier-markdown-kit/will` | The Will/1 grammar (a separate, optional standard): the markers around an agent's intent regions. |
| `rapier-markdown-kit/assets` | The picture appendix: the reference definitions a document's pictures live in. It never decodes a picture. |
| `rapier-markdown-kit/style.css` | The reference style: type, lists, tables, tasks, pictures and the document's other markup, scoped to `.md-render`. |
| `rapier-markdown-kit/rapier-ledger` | The MIT edit ledger: `openLedger`, replay, authorship, selective Undo, offline `merge`, three-way `mergeText`, and the carried parts. |
| `rapier-markdown-kit/pdf` | `attachPdfSource`: attach the exact source to a PDF without rewriting its pages; `readPdfPageCount`. |
| `rapier-markdown-kit/ledger/carried` | Checked optional parts for pages and saved Markdown. |
| `rapier-markdown-kit` | Named exports from layout, marks, model, Will, assets and render, plus the `ledger` namespace. Import `createTypography` from `/typography`; the root does not export that ambiguous name. |

The canonical inline form is ordinary HTML inside Markdown. CSS support varies; the host's font metrics still
determine line layout (below).

## Read a parsed document

`projectMarkdown` copies the tokens from your completed parse into JSON data. Pass the exact source and revision
captured for that parse, and a grammar identity that includes its parser, plugins and options. The function does not
parse again. Project before renderer hooks mutate the tokens; the resulting snapshot is detached from those later
changes. Import this optional subpath only where you need it; the package's main entry does not import it.

```js
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it';
import {rapierMarkdown} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/markdown-it';
import {projectMarkdown, projectionMatches} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/parsed';

const source = '# Plan\n\nShips **Friday**.\n';
const revision = 7;
const options = {html: true};
const grammar = {id: 'my-app-markdown-1', options, plugins: ['rapierMarkdown']};
const md = new MarkdownIt(options).use(rapierMarkdown);
const env = {};
const tokens = md.parse(source, env); // The same tokens can feed your renderer.
const parsed = projectMarkdown({source, revision, grammar, tokens, env, complete: true});
const json = JSON.stringify(parsed);
console.log(projectionMatches(parsed, {source, revision, grammar})); // true
```

Change the grammar identity when its implementation changes. Grammar options must be JSON data; describe a custom
rule or renderer by its identity, not by a function. If your parse excludes opening front matter, pass `bodyOffset`
from that split and keep `source` as the full original document. Token line maps must remain relative to the parsed body.

The source binding uses SHA-256 over its UTF-16LE code units, including BOM, original line endings and isolated
surrogates. `span` ranges are half-open UTF-16 offsets into that source. A span with `scope: 'lines'` covers the token's
source lines, including container prefixes and the final line ending. Inline delimiters and generated tokens without
recorded ranges have `span: null`; `coverage` and `omissions` report these missing ranges. Never infer an exact inline
edit boundary from a containing line span.

Recorded `meta.mdLayoutSource` positions are translated from the parser's normalized body into the same original
UTF-16 source coordinates and labeled `unit: 'utf16'`. Their marker text and any reason for an unmapped target remain
with the layout record. Other JSON metadata retains the grammar's values; internal probe identities are not exported.

The projection includes canonical token content, attributes, JSON metadata and reference, abbreviation and footnote
definitions. It omits original source gaps, interpreted front matter, rendered HTML and geometry, decoded pictures,
final heading IDs, and evaluated Will permissions. Non-JSON token metadata becomes `null` with a counted omission.
Token strings remain document data for your existing renderer and sanitizer. `projectionMatches` checks currentness;
it does not authenticate a projection received from another party or authorize an edit. Source transactions, Will,
Undo and Save stay with their existing owners.

## Refined paragraphs

The existing comment expresses the paragraph's intent without storing font-dependent line breaks:

```md
Words stay in their original source. <!--md-layout:v1 align=justify hyphens=auto hanging=on-->
```

`align=justify` alone keeps native justification. With `hyphens=auto`, the browser adapter chooses a paragraph-wide
plan using the same pinned Pretext analysis, shaping and actual-font authority as picture wrapping. It prefers
whole words, bounds ordinary spaces to 60–180% of their natural advance, permits at most two consecutive
discretionary endings, and starts the final line with a whole word. A short final line costs more; the final line
is never stretched. Authored compound hyphens are ordinary break opportunities, distinct from discretionary ones.
In very narrow measures, bounded spaces can leave some ragged edges. There is no paragraph-length switch.

Automatic cuts keep at least three graphemes on each side, with at most one automatic split per word. ASCII words
under `en` and `en-US` use the included Kuiken/Plain TeX pattern data and exceptions. Other English regions,
non-ASCII words and other admitted languages ask the browser's offline hyphenator for legal positions. That path
requires native `hyphenate-limit-chars` support; otherwise the paragraph stays native. Available dictionaries and
their divisions depend on the host. The included American patterns are a deliberate alternative to native data,
not a promise of identical opportunities in every browser. No language or font data is downloaded.

The projection displays a hyphen-minus from the affected text face, measured by Pretext as part of the whole
prefix. It never adds a source hyphen. Explicit authored `hyphenate-character` stays native. With `hanging=on`,
measured punctuation extends only into available unclipped margins, by at most half an em. Refinement adds no
letter tracking; authored supported letter spacing remains part of its shaping contract.

Here `root` is your rendered document element in a browser. Keep the event handlers and scheduled work with that element’s lifetime.

```js
import {createTypography} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/typography';

const refinement = createTypography();
await document.fonts.ready;
let active = true, frame = 0;
function update() {
  cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = 0;
  if (active && refinement.apply(root).pending) frame = requestAnimationFrame(update);
}
update();
function afterClipboard() {
  if (active && refinement.clearSelection(root)) {
    cancelAnimationFrame(frame); frame = requestAnimationFrame(update);
  }
}
for (const event of ['copy', 'cut']) document.addEventListener(event, afterClipboard, true);
// On a width change, call update() again. Source/style/font changes are revalidated.
// Before native editing or consuming this disposable DOM projection:
refinement.clear(root);
// When retiring the root:
active = false;
cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
for (const event of ['copy', 'cut']) document.removeEventListener(event, afterClipboard, true);
refinement.retire(root);
```

`apply()` works on visible paragraphs and yields at completed preparation phases or word batches after an 8 ms
allowance. A single native shaping call can exceed that allowance; it is not a hard execution deadline. Pending
paragraphs remain native and readable. Each continuation revalidates source, style and font authority, and chooses
lines at the current width only after all required metrics finish. `{all:true}` performs the same complete work
synchronously for explicit capture or a print host with an established content width. Width changes reuse current measured geometry, and unchanged break
topology reuses projection nodes. Bind font loading, completion and failure to `invalidateFonts(document)` and
schedule `apply()`; a changed font generation removes stale projections before new preparation.

The adapter retains original text, semantic elements and listeners, backward selections, hard breaks, protected
code/nowrap atoms, NBSP, SHY and Unicode source coordinates. `clearSelection()` restores selected inline trees
before native clipboard capture; schedule refinement afterward as above. The editor and complete exported pages
bind this lifecycle themselves. Active editing/composition stays native. Unsupported
scripts, direction, shaping controls, initials and picture-flow paragraphs also stay native. The current adapter
admits horizontal LTR Latin, Greek, Cyrillic and common/inherited characters on Chrome/Chromium; native font
coverage and language support still apply. A font-family name is never a substitute for a loaded actual face.

Complete exported pages carry the same single module graph, CSP nonce, offline language data and font lifecycle.
Their readiness promise completes after the visible refinement queue; scrolling refines newly visible paragraphs.
Before print, an authored paper size supplies the fixed content width and all paragraphs finish synchronously.
Automatic-paper browser printing clears the projection and uses native CSS: `beforeprint` may still report the
screen viewport rather than the selected paper. Scoped fragments and `scripts:false` output also retain native CSS. The American data's separate permissive notice and exact provenance accompany the kit;
Pretext retains its own complete notices. These vendor notices are not replaced by the kit's MIT grant.

## One inline typography form

```md
Plain prose needs no typography markup.

A <span style="font-size:13.5pt;color:#175dc4">precise **phrase**</span>.

## <span style="font-size:9.25pt;font-family:serif">Still a semantic H2</span>

<span style="font-size:18px;color:#175dc4;font-family:&quot;Coastal Text&quot;">An offline custom run</span>

[font:Coastal Text]: data:font/woff2;base64,<font-bytes> '{"family":"Coastal Text","sourceId":"f0123456789abcdef01234567"}'
```

The font bytes and identity in that last example are placeholders; a host derives identity from admitted bytes.
A family name alone is not a portable font. Default prose needs no font reference. Custom faces keep the existing
font-data authority, including a name that collides with a factory face.

`typography.normalize({size, color, family})` validates a style. `typography.wrap(style, inlineMarkdown)` writes one
inline span; split block selections and keep their `#`, list markers and separators outside. `typography.parseStyle`
returns only admitted facts. `typography.install(md)` installs that interpretation on the caller's markdown-it
parser, and `typographySourceRanges(source, md)` reports original UTF-16 wrapper ranges through that parser.
These calls neither mutate the source nor load resources. The installer also reads already-authored color and
font comments into the same facts; an ordinary open/save must preserve their bytes, not rewrite them as spans.

Sizes accept positive decimal `pt`/`px`, at most 12 fractional digits, up to 1638pt/2184px; 96px = 72pt. New values
use lowercase units and omit insignificant zeros. Colors become lowercase six-digit RGB hex; opaque integer
RGB CSSOM values are also read. Families are one validated name, an unquoted CSS generic, or an existing preset
stack. `sans`, `serif`, `mono`, `system`, `hand` are reserved choice aliases, not quoted custom identities. Styles
are bounded to 4096 characters, 32 declarations and 64 paired levels. Invalid declarations and unknown properties
are ignored; invalid/unclosed style strings admit no facts. Inner spans override individual properties. An editor
clearing a selection removes that property's overrides and preserves the surrounding words' styles.

Keep each opener with its first words and each closer with its last words. Soft/hard breaks may stay inside one paragraph; blank lines cannot. An opener alone on a line can become a raw HTML block.
With inline HTML enabled, the new form preserves words, emphasis,
links and heading rank; GitHub strips the styles, and HTML-disabled readers may show the tags. Rapier's **Copy
markdown without typography** removes recognized wrappers while retaining semantic Markdown and literal code.
Its separate Pandoc/Quarto copy option writes bracketed spans deliberately; Pandoc HTML carries the CSS, but
ordinary LaTeX and native DOCX styling do not follow automatically.

Rapier's own Word adapter writes native run properties, rounding to the nearest half-point with positive ties up
and refusing results outside 1–3276 half-points. The unchanged DOCX source carrier keeps original decimals and units;
native import reports represented direct-run/character-style sizes without repeating document or paragraph defaults
as inline marks. It does not reproduce an arbitrary Word style sheet. HTML and print/PDF retain the same admitted facts at the default reference
unit, independent of editor zoom. No mapping claims identical glyphs or line breaks across applications.

See the original [typography guidance](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/blob/main/docs/markdown-standard.md#inline-typography),
[CommonMark raw HTML](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#raw-html), [CSS absolute units](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-values-4/#absolute-lengths),
[Pandoc spans](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#extension-bracketed_spans) and [Quarto spans](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html#divs-and-spans).
Those specifications retain their own licenses.

## Render with the reference style

Import `rapier-markdown-kit/style.css` in a CSS-aware bundler, or copy that file beside your HTML and
link it with `<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">`. Put rendered content inside
`<main class="md-render">`. The sheet follows the system theme; `data-md-theme="light"` or `"dark"`
on that root chooses one. Its `--md-*` properties are defined by the sheet itself. Geist and Geist Mono
are named font families with system fallbacks; no font or external asset is fetched by the sheet.

The example below renders trusted Markdown with `markdown-it` and the kit's readers: run
`npm install rapier-markdown-kit markdown-it@15`, save it as `render.mjs`, run `node render.mjs` and open
`styled.html`, which uses only `style.css`. It shows core Markdown, GFM tables, an aligned paragraph, a sized
picture, a precise combined run, a semantic heading and a page break; tasks, footnotes and diagrams are the caller's plugins. The full markup
contract is [Reference style](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/blob/main/docs/markdown-standard.md#reference-style).

<!-- reference-style-example -->
```js
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it';
import {rapierMarkdown} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/markdown-it';
import {formatLayout} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/layout';
import {TEXT_COLOR_NAMES, typography, formatColorRun, formatPageBreak} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/marks';
import {readFile, writeFile} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {pathToFileURL} from 'node:url';

const md = new MarkdownIt({html: true, linkify: true}).use(rapierMarkdown);

export function renderReferenceDocument(source) {
  return md.render(source);
}

export const exampleSource = [
  '# A document everywhere',
  '',
  'One paragraph with **weight**, *emphasis*, `inline code` and a [link](https://example.com).',
  '',
  '## ' + typography.wrap({size: '21.5pt', family: 'serif'}, 'Lists and tables'),
  '',
  '1. First numbered item',
  '2. Second numbered item',
  '   - A nested bullet',
  '   - Another nested bullet',
  '',
  '| Subject | Detail |',
  '| --- | --- |',
  '| Style | Shared by editor and page |',
  '',
  '> A quoted paragraph.',
  '',
  '### A little code',
  '',
  '~~~text',
  'plain code',
  '~~~',
  '',
  'A centered paragraph.' + formatLayout({align: 'center'}),
  '',
  'A ' + formatColorRun(TEXT_COLOR_NAMES.blue, 'blue phrase') + ' keeps its color.',
  '',
  'And ' + typography.wrap({size: '13.5pt', color: '#175dc4', family: 'serif'}, '**precise words**') + ' keep their emphasis.',
  '',
  '![A square](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAQAAAC1HAwCAAAAC0lEQVR42mP8/x8AAwMCAO+aDAkAAAAASUVORK5CYII=)' + formatLayout({width: 45, align: 'center'}),
  '',
  '<details open><summary>Details</summary><p>A little more to read.</p></details>',
  '',
  formatPageBreak(),
  '',
  'The next printed page.',
].join('\n');

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) {
  await writeFile('style.css', await readFile(new URL(import.meta.resolve('rapier-markdown-kit/style.css'))));
  await writeFile('styled.html', '<!doctype html><html lang="en"><meta charset="utf-8">' +
    '<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1"><title>Shared style</title>' +
    '<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"><main class="md-render">' +
    renderReferenceDocument(exampleSource) + '</main></html>');
  console.log('Wrote styled.html and style.css');
}
```

## Example

Save this as `example.mjs` in the folder you installed into and run `node example.mjs`. It validates
the fragments' source custody and prints the resulting line count and height for its supplied measurements.

```js
import {parseLayout} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/layout';
import {parseProfile, pictureSlices, createPreparationScope, flowLines, mapFragment} from 'rapier-markdown-kit/model';
const {loadDocuments, installMeasurer} = await import(new URL(
  './dist/kit/conformance/measurer.mjs', import.meta.resolve('rapier-markdown-kit/package.json')));

// Text metrics: the widths the conformance documents recorded in Rapier's own browser, standing in
// for a font shaper so the example runs anywhere (see "What the host supplies").
installMeasurer(loadDocuments());

// 1. Parse the layout comment a picture carries.
const layout = parseLayout('<!--md-layout:v1 width=40% wrap=around x=25%-->');
// => {width: 40, wrap: 'around', x: 25}

// 2. The picture's shape: the occupancy descriptor Rapier's exports carry beside a picture
// (`data-rapier-occupancy`, one left-right pair per horizontal band), placed as obstacles.
const profile = parseProfile('0.1-0.9|0.2-0.8|0.3-0.7');
const obstacles = pictureSlices(profile, /* x */ 0, /* y */ 0, /* width */ 120, /* height */ 90);

// 3. Plan the lines of a paragraph around those obstacles.
const text = 'This anchor paragraph carries enough ordinary prose', font = 'normal 400 17.6px Geist, system-ui, sans-serif';
const preparation = createPreparationScope(), paragraph = {};
const flow = preparation.prepare(paragraph, [{text, font, letterSpacing: 0}], {language: 'en'});
if (!flow) throw new Error('The host could not prepare this paragraph');
const plan = flowLines(flow, /* column width */ 300, /* top */ 0, obstacles, /* line height */ 20, /* min slot */ 40);
// Each line carries its own x, y and width, and the text fragments laid into it.
if (!plan || !preparation.current(flow)) throw new Error('No current plan');
let end = 0;
for (const line of plan.lines) for (const fragment of line.fragments) {
  const mapped = mapFragment(text, fragment);
  if (!mapped || mapped.start < end || text.slice(end, mapped.start).trim()) throw new Error('Unmapped source');
  end = mapped.end;
}
if (text.slice(end).trim()) throw new Error('Unmapped source tail');
console.log('lines:', plan.lines.length, 'height:', plan.height);
```

The block's `text-align` is the ninth argument (`'start'` by default). Native balanced headings retain native
wrapping: the current rich line-range API does not identify every legal balancing candidate. A picture moves a
block's words only where its outline meets them: when no line of the
block, laid and aligned in the whole column as with no picture, meets an obstacle, the plan is that layout (`x` 0, the
column's width); otherwise every line flows around the obstacles.

## What the host supplies

Rich preparation measures text through one pinned Pretext graph. It needs a global
`OffscreenCanvas` (or a DOM `document`) whose `getContext('2d')` has a settable `font` and a
`measureText(text)` returning `{width}`. A browser has one already; in Node, put those two members
in front of the host's actual shaper and admit its fonts before preparation. The example replays historical
measurements instead; an unrecorded query falls back to summing single characters. That fallback demonstrates API
execution only and does not qualify kerning, ligatures, complex scripts or actual browser line selection.

Create one `createPreparationScope(document)` for a host document in the same measurement realm. Call
`scope.prepare(owner, items, {whiteSpace, wordBreak, language})` with a stable paragraph owner and original rich
items; omitted document support is available for declared Node measurement hosts. Text items accept
`{text, font, letterSpacing?, break?: 'normal' | 'never', extraWidth?}`; box items accept `{width}`. Paragraph
`whiteSpace` is `normal` or `pre-wrap`, and `wordBreak` is `normal` or `keep-all`. `language` is the content language,
not the interface locale. Mixed run languages require native fallback. The scope retains owners weakly and reuses
preparation across widths. Changes to exact text, item shaping settings or language require a new preparation.

The returned handle is opaque. Pass it to `flowLines`, or retain the original ranges from
`layoutNextRichInlineLineRange` for `materializeRichInlineLineRange`. Materialized fragments give `itemIndex`,
`sourceStart` and `sourceEnd` in UTF-16 offsets of that item's **original** text; `mapFragment(originalText, fragment)`
provides the shared display-to-source mapping. `gapItemIndex` names the source style for a collapsed gap. Never decode
range cursors as old segment/grapheme fields, resegment text to interpret them, JSON-serialize or deep-freeze the
handle. Storage segments and emergency overflow advances are not a list of legal breaks.

`scope.current(handle)` checks the shared actual-font authority before projection. Bind font loading, completion and
failure to `scope.invalidateFonts()` and schedule reflow. Actual face identity, descriptors and status detect
same-name replacement and invalidate the vendor's metric cache as well as prepared handles. Width changes do
neither. Call `scope.forget(owner)` when a block stops participating. One imported graph owns the realm's vendor
metrics; another bundle or copied vendor tree cannot share that authority. Call `scope.retire()` when replacing or
retiring a projection scope, so both its handles and the shared vendor metrics are retired. This retains the
document's known custom-family history, allowing a missing previously declared face to be refused instead of
silently measured through a fallback. Only the owner replacing the whole document calls
`scope.retire({documentChanged: true})`, which also resets that document's expected-family history.

The browser adapter calls `supportsRichStyle(style, language)` and refuses settings the pinned API cannot represent.
The API has no independent controls for kerning, OpenType features, variation settings, optical sizing, word spacing
or mixed item language; a matching font-family string alone is not proof of matching actual font data. Unsupported
settings, unavailable or failed faces, complex objects, authored `br`, preserved-whitespace DOM paragraphs and
balanced headings keep selectable native DOM. Direct prepared-text hosts can use `pre-wrap` with original CRLF and
hard breaks. The reference combines browser-derived break tables and Canvas metrics with JavaScript flow. The DOM
adapter admits Chrome/Chromium profiles; Firefox, WebKit and Chrome on iOS retain native DOM. It does not invoke live
DOM line selection or promise identical pixels in other engines.
Editor soft-break source tokens and generated-content shells stay native. The semantic export resolves verified
soft-break tokens to ordinary rendered spaces through its existing owner before wrapping; its source carrier keeps
the original Markdown unchanged.
Ordinary picture flow keeps its greedy policy instead of the reference sheet's generic `pretty` preference;
explicit authored inline `text-wrap:pretty` retains native wrapping. No native pretty optimization is claimed.
A lone Latin, Greek or Cyrillic word prefix, including an authored no-break-space group, may defer to a later
wider picture-side slot on the same row when the public engine output fits the entire group there. Decorated
atoms, mixed-item words, punctuation, discretionary breaks and next-row placement retain the engine policy.

`md-layout:v1` remains semantic and engine-independent. No plan or font-dependent pixel carrier is saved. Offline
complete pages load their admitted embedded faces before enhanced wrapping; fragments and `scripts:false` pages
retain native wrapping. Fonts and codecs remain explicit host capabilities as described above.

`alphaProfile(image)` samples a decoded `<img>` through a canvas, so it needs a browser. Without
one, read the saved descriptor with `parseProfile`, or sample the picture with your own image
library. `polygonProfile` and `rasterTiltProfile` are plain geometry.

The appendix API accepts a markdown-it-compatible parser factory from the caller
(`parseAssets(source, factory)`, or once through `configureParser`). Comment-aware edit history
also carries Rapier's pinned Markdown parser and canonical configuration. A fresh synchronous
ledger reader initializes that parser when needed, so accepted comment history can reopen in a
worker or standalone package. A parser already configured by the host is reused.

## Conformance

```sh
node node_modules/rapier-markdown-kit/dist/kit/conformance/run.mjs
```

Thirteen small documents, each with the line boxes Rapier's own export produced for it. **Preservation**: every
layout comment round-trips exactly (12 of 12 that carry one). **Presentation** compares the plan with historical
measurements and reports real-trace hits separately from character-sum misses (`dist/kit/conformance/README.md`).
Its historical line counts are not a current-engine or font-shaping acceptance gate.
`--impl path/to/module.mjs` runs another implementation against the same documents; `--tolerance 2` sets the pixel
tolerance.
